top_review: Any Bruder Toy makes the best* birthday gift for boys/girls!!! Mine love how you can steer/drive the Defender! Yes! On the bottom of the SUV there is a steering wheel. Open up the sunroof and insert in slot- the front wheels steer. SO COOL! So impressed!!!If you’re a Classic Land Rover Defender Fan - this is a ”hoot”. Good German quality toy!My nephew LOVES his Bruder trucks. I got him the Mack dumptruck for his birthday last year, the big backhoe for Christmas, and the Land Rover for his 3rd birthday. He loves that the doors and hood open so he can put toy friends inside, and the dump truck is still good as new even with a rambunctious two year old playing with it for a year now. The moving buckets on the backhoe have held up great too playing in the sandbox and inside. The steering wheel on the roof of the Land Rover (can be removed and stored underneath the truck) is a great touch and he figured out how to steer it quickly! These vehicles are well-built and incredibly realistic, and they are strong yet lightweight plastic so they can be used indoors or out. He will be getting a Bruder fire truck for Christmas!Good toy for teaching how to park a trailer. It is made of plastic, so won't last forever.The plastic is durable, which turns out to be a good thing. Upon arrival, the back door was pushed way to far inside and I had to pull with quite a bit of effort to snap it back out (so that it can open outwards). Unfortunately, it seems to go back inside too easily so the kiddo's need to take it to mom or dad to pull it back out.The tires are soft rubber which adds to the realistic features.The tailgate on the trailer opens easily and has held quite a bit of horses, atv's, dinosaurs, people, marbles, and anything else that fits.We haven't successfully opened the sunroof to fit the steering extension in there (it's snapped closed pretty tight). I'm hesitant to push to hard because it seems like it'll break before it opens.There's no instructions on how everything opens, just pictures on the box (helpful to some degree).Overall, I give it 4 stars.PROs: Seems durable... Kids enjoy it (ages 12, 4, 3)... nothing has broken... lots of doors that open easily (side doors, hood, trailer)... The trailer fits easily on the trailer hitch (not a mom and dad job like some other toys)... lightweight.CONs: Some of the doors are extremely difficult to open (sunroof, backdoor when pushed in too far).I would order it again.Grandson L shouted as he opened his gift that "this was the best gift ever" . The only problem was that the motorcycle broke within the first 4 days he owned it. He was so excited that he had a car just like his dad's Discovery car. Why would the product not hold up to a 4 year old. He is not a kid to throw his toys. The cute little steering wheel had no instructions that it was stored under the car. But that was misplaced right away. It is a very cute car, everything opens and he loved looking at the motor etc. There are just a few weaknesses.I like this toy very very much... may be even more than my son does. This is an excellent miniature version of the iconic Land Rover Defender SUV. This is made entirely of plastic. The attention to detail is impressive. Both the driver and passenger doors open as well as the back door! The hood pops up and there is even a hood stand!! Both front wheel are connected to the steering wheel such that if you rotate the steering in any direction, the front wheels actually turn! But that is not the most amazing thing in this mini Land Rover. The best feature of this replica is the independent wheel suspension for all 4 wheels. If you drive this over a toy soldier for example, you will notice that the wheel directly over the soldier lifts slightly up to accommodate the soldier while all the other 3 wheels are still maintaining contact with the ground. This is what Land Rovers are famous for and what all the real off-road capable vehicles display. I was just amazed to find that they would put this much amount of work inside a toy at this price range. Bruder totally rocks!For the record, I do not approve of driving toy Land Rovers over toy soldiers.If you are shopping for the kind of kid who appreciates the finer details in his/her toys (for example, cannot spend enough time opening/closing the doors and windows of the toy car, popping the hood and trunk, turning the tiny steering wheel, etc) then this will be a big hit. It looks incredibly real, has about as many movable/interactive parts as you can imagine, has a really cool set of shocks for realistic offloading, and incorporates one of the more intelligent additions I have ever seen in a toy car: a removable steering wheel that detaches from the bottom of the car, clicks in to the axles through the sunroof, and allows the lucky recipient of this gift to steer the car from above without having to cram their fingers through the drivers side window to try and steer the wheel and move the car at the same time. Pretty sweet if you ask me...I was once a young guy who loved toy cars and would like to think I played with enough of them growing up to give a qualified recommendation on this one.Was really disappointed when this arrived, especially after reading such good reviews! I paid £43 and was expecting a good quality product. Instead it feels very cheap. The horse is okay, but the jeep and trailer are made of flimsy plastic. The tyres are of a good quality though.I think my 3 year old would have liked it but for the money I spent I expected better quality.I would have been happy to have paid £15 for this toy.We bought this for my son aged 2 1/2 and it is still a hit with him 18 months later. The detail on the land rover is fantastic, it's so realistic. It has proper suspension and doors that open. Bruder sells figures that will fit in the seats, but duplo figures work just as well. The land rover can even be steered as it comes with a little steering wheel that is attached through a sun roof, so it can be 'driven' around by holding the roof as normal, or by using the extra steering wheel.It has stood up well to constant use but one of the doors and a wing mirror did break off. Thankfully Bruder sell replacements parts though so we were able to get a kit with an extra back door, side doors and bonnet which have given it a new lease of life. Bruder toys are quite expensive but they are so well built they are worth it. A firm favourite with my son for years.Land Rover is of the highest quality. Functions like a detachable steering wheel, connected via the sunroof, allows better controlled driving. Suspension, opening doors bonnet bonnet further adds to the realism. Not forgetting a useful full towbar, which brings me to the potential negatives. Although the towbar holds a trailer securely, I'm not sure it'll withstand constant fiction uncoupling yet still maintain a firm connection or will it wear and become easy to accidentally detach. And I've had a quick try but unable to get a Bruder figure to sit in the front. Certainly wouldn't be easy for a child. Okay small stuff aside. Every part not just looking like a decent toy, appearance, quality and detail better than my 1/18th scale replica plus at 1/16 it's 11% bigger :-DAn excellent product, well made - and not just fun for kids; I bought this for a friend who was having trouble working out his technique for reversing his 2 axle trailer; a new experience for him. There's an extra steering wheel that pops in through the sunroof so you can steer it easily from the top, et voila - he could practice his reversing safely on the dining table - or simply have a great toy for when his little grandson visits.One thing bemuses me, however, is why is it £33.13 on Amazon UK whilst it's €283.99 (£233.52) on Amazon FR - Doh…?My 2 year old loves his Land Rover so much that he takes it everywhere with him (to sleep, brush his teeth, to nursery). It is robust, he bashes it against his other cars and it is still intact. Looks just like the real thing. The doors and bonnet open, and the extended steering wheel is a cool addition. Very happy!

title: Victorinox-Swiss-Army-Cutlery Fibrox Pro Slicing Knife, Round Tip, 10-Inch
description: A TRUSTED FAVORITE Preferred by both home chefs and culinary professionals, the 10" Victorinox Fibrox Pro Slicing Knife can handle nearly every kitchen task imaginable. Crafted with a comfortable handle, superior weight and balance, and a razor sharp blade with a round tip that rarely requires re-sharpening, this knife is an essential tool for every kitchen. KEY FEATURES High-quality, lightweight European steel. Handle design reduces hand and wrist fatigue. Fit for slicing both firm and soft meats. Long, straight blade with round tip for maximized cutting performance. Non-slip, textured handle for a secure and comfortable grip no matter the hand size. National Sanitary Foundation (NSF) approved and dishwasher safe. CARE AND USE Be good to your knives and they’ll be good to you. Following these simple guidelines will ensure that you get the longest life out of your knife! CLEANING Victorinox Swiss Army recommends washing all knives by hand. For best results, hand wash your knives with a soapy cloth and dry immediately. While Fibrox Pro knives are dishwasher safe, we recommend hand washing as dishwashers are designed to spray water at a relatively high pressure, which can jostle the silverware and cause the knives to collide, dulling the edge. SHARPENING For optimum performance, knives should be honed after every couple of uses. Proper and frequent use of a honing steel will keep your knives sharper and performing at their best. FORMERLY FORSCHNER In 1937 Victorinox began selling cutlery in America through a Connecticut distributor called R.H. Forschner & Co. A well-known manufacturer of butcher scales, Forschner soon became the exclusive U.S. distributor for Victorinox knives, and was the name by which Victorinox knives were known.

top_review: This is a great knife for the price. It’s sharp and easy to handle. The weight is just right. One of my favorite knives.This is a super cool knife. It is super long which makes cutting through things very easy. It is amazingly sharp too so be careful! Definitely a worthwhile purchase.Used it the day I got it to cut up Smoked Baby Back Ribs and it cut through them like butter. Great Quality. The handle has a great feel and is not slippery when wet.When this knife is brand new, it will slice anything you throw at it with ease. However, after a year of using it on all wooden cutting boards and cutting only meat and occasionally bread, I found I could barely cut a sirloin roast. I had noticed it seemed to be losing its edge and finally I got my honing rods out, flipped it over to look at the edge and could visibly see how out of straight it was. I honed it back into shape quickly and its like new again. I love this knife, but I you do need to sharpen it regularly. I only used it a dozed times throughout the year so I never imagined it would dull like that, but the blade is Very thin so I think that's maybe the issue. In any case, I do recommend it as it's great for the price. Just remember to sharpen it when it starts to dull...Still sharp, handle is still perfect, no nicks or burrs. Excellent quality. As with any knife, let it do the work. If the blade flexes while cutting you are probably trying to force a cut or go too quickly.Fulfills it's purpose admirably.Oh my, sharp, such smooth even slices.I bought this to slice meat for jerky, best buy since my dehydrator, maybe better.I started to make jerky for high protein, low carb, low sugar snacks. If you've never had fresh warm jerky, you have missed a true treat. Home made beats the packaged brands less cost, and allows for a variety of meats and flavors (beef, chicken, pork, spicy, teriyaki.....).I Tried it on two eye of round roasts, as I was anxious, the first was chilled firm, but not as solid I usually had to for the knife that came with my old slicer set.The difference was like night and day, smooth cuts, no sawing. Cuts were uniform, no blade flexing making uneven spots, cut all the way through (horizontally under the meat), no tapering, didn't have to move the roast to orient to a trailing edge. finished slicing in 1/3 the time too. Then when I would have had to switch blades to trim to size, once again this knife did the job, cutting like soft butter, and because of the length I got some fantastic pieces.The second roast was a bit firmer, I tested other cuts, first I took rounds off the thick end, even tried some free hand (with out the slicer form, just this knife), and finished with the slicer unit, the knife started sharp and remained sharp. I even though about donning a cutting glove, as I got near the end of my task, with the meat being about twice the width of the slice.This knife also was great with some left over turkey breast, I can hardly wait to use it on the holiday ham.If there was any downside, it was the packaging, a plastic bubble, that while allowing a good view of the knife and keeping the edges protected during shipping, may lack the elegance of a box that some people may desire. It also lacked an edge guard, but with only adults in the kitchen, it is not an issue for me.Personally I would rather have a good knife, the package doesn't matter when it in use, and that's what this is. A very good knife.Final notes - the Fibrox handle was very comfortable at different cutting angles. It has a dual sided Granton blade. The blade is well balanced and centered in the handle, and should be usable right or left handed. For a 12 inch blade it is very light and maneuverable. The blade is Swiss made, and NSE certified. It is supposed to be dishwasher safe, though I would be sure to place it in a way other items won't bump the cutting edge.Cut 13# of rib steak with ease! This knife made cutting, thus packing the rib steak easy. I can buy these steaks at bulk for $5 # cheaper, then vacuum pack and freeze. After getting 14 steaks out of the slab, 1.5" thick each, all looking like a butcher cut, and freezing them; my cost of the knife on this first round was paid for by the savings of the steak. I have other knifes that are not nearly as efficient and effective as this knife. Highly recommend this product.Wonderful for slicing roast beef!This is a scary knife: big, fairly weighty and extremely sharp. It is quite long with a blade length of 29 cm and remarkably wide at 4 cm. I bought it as a carving knife as recommended by several reviewers who rated it very high. However, I found it messy when cutting a joint of pork and it was hopeless at cutting through crackling. It actually is described as a edge slicing knife and not a carving knife and this is really a better description. It is the wider width than standard that allows such straight cutting, while the sharpness of the blade makes such a difference. This difference in description (slicing knife) is important as while it might be great for carving more solid textured meat, for a general purpose carving knife a serrated edged knife would be better. Indeed, the Victorinox carving knife with serrated edge proved to be a great Christmas present for my son-in-law and perhaps I should have bought the same. That knife not only cut through all manner of meats, but it did so with great accuracy and produced very thin and uniform slices as required. However, for fine textured meat the Granton slicing knife will be splendid and I find it a brilliant bread knife giving a really straight cut with no crumbs.I bought this a gift for my dad to replace an ancient scalloped knife that had started to arch along the blade edge through many years of sharpening.The first thing to mention is the size. At 12inches and a hefty height o the blade you're going to want to be confident with kitchen knives before using (or the person you're buying it for does). The second thing is that this knife comes SHARP from the factory. You can take it out and use straight away without having to refine the edge in any way. The handle is a textured plastic which gives a good solid grip.In use the knife performs very well. A large joint of meat can easily be sliced thinly, the length allowing a single cut to be made, rather than having to use a sawing motion, with can pull the meat apart. Obviously the sharpness helps here, so you'll need to keep that fine edge. It also worked very well as a bread knife, slicing through hard crusty loaves and fluffy white bread with ease.Its worth noting that the size of the blade means that for fiddly jobs, such as getting into the nooks and crannies of a roast chicken, this knife wont be as useful as a smaller Sabatier type knife. Not a criticism, as its obviously not designed for that job, but worth noting.It is a long thin blade and flexable it also has a rounded tip which means it is good for slicing ham although it is not technically a carving knife it will carve meat nicely though some may find it a bit long you can carve thin slices which is more difficult with a traditional carving knife.I also find it good for slicing sides of smoked salmon where you really need to cut thin slices. Its reasonably priced now that its been reduced by 34% and you would be hard pushed to find something better for the price.I bought this knife to carve meat - particularly large joints of meat. I have found it easy to sharpen and very effective - mine can cut roast pork with the crackling on though I normally take that off and use scissors. It is a large knife but this makes it easy to use - at least for me. I find the handle easy to hold and it provides a stable and precise grip.After buying a Victorinox bread knife, which I was delighted with I purchased this knife as a carving knife. Again the blade is extra long allowing a good length of saw cut. The knife has a slim blade and razor edge making carving of all meats a pleasure. Our Christmas turkey has never been so well carved, even to almost shaving. Highly recommend this knife for all carving duties.

Since the seller indicated these drapes aren’t true blackout within the description, I purchased a blackout reflective panel that adheres to the window with Velcro adhesive strips and prior to hanging the drapes, applied it to the glass.I’ve never liked the texture of blackout drapes as they feel stiff and plasticky so I opted for a solution that allowed for a richer aesthetic. Obviously these drapes remain closed since the glass has been fitted with a heat reflective panel in order to keep out the desert heat here in Las Vegas, where I live.I am extremely happy with these beautiful velvet drapes and love how they hang, feel, look PLUS they deliver exactly what I was hoping for.The color is perfect and I was torn between several options. I took several weeks of looking at different types of fabrics, colors and at every seller on Amazon to finally make my decision. I was originally going to use a linen fabric with blackout panels sewn into the backing but when I came across these I began to rethink it altogether. I could not be more satisfied with my choice to change the fabric to velvet and to go with a color I’d not considered at all. The stone blue is very forgiving as it has a slightly green hue and is a sneaky “color shifting” shade that would fit just about any pallet. The room is predominantly furnished with dark blues and a plush multicolored area rug with a cream/off white background, the carpet’s muted blues, greens and pastel reddish pink touches just look lovely with these rich velvet, flowing drapes.Upon arrival I threw these in the washer, I bought 2 packages so all 4 panels went in on the “bulky”cycle with warm water. Since they’re polyester I expected no shrinkage. I dried them partially, leaving them slightly damp and hung them immediately. This technique works on heavier fabrics to remove most wrinkles as the weight itself aids in removing fold marks. I employed a hand held steamer (if you don’t own one, get one as it’ll change your life) to get out any stubborn wrinkles. I cannot imagine a better result. You don’t need an expensive steamer as they all use the same technology and I use it frequently instead of an iron.One thing I noticed while setting out on this journey of drape buying online, is that the same exact products are sold by many merchants and prices are definitely not consistent. top_review: I have bought two of this set and have many of the Garry Potter sets. For ne, thus is such a show piece that I display it and everyone wants to talk about it when they see it. It is retired, so grab it while you can.The box came in a iffy condition making me think it was used. But it wasn’t so I am happy. So if you’re collecting these or looking for just the box, maybe not get it. But if you’re just looking to build the set and or collect the actual lego set itself when built, it’s perfect.This set was fun to build, and pretty straight-forward too. The pictures-only manual only led me astray once (the strangely fiddly hinges for the top of the tower, that didn't seem to line up at first...), and it's strangely addictive, as some parts were mystifying while being put together, and only made sense once you actually put them into the rest of the model.I did have a couple of minor niggles: I was missing a piece! A single, one-piece block, that appeared in the instructions, but was absent from the set. It was for the base of one of the buttresses on the outside of the hall, and while I ended up with a couple of pieces among the extras I could have used, I didn't know at the time if they were needed for something else! There was another case of one of the pieces being a different color than the manual indicated, but that was it, apart from that, it all went together pretty nicely.The finished model is wonderful, even if not all the bits seem built entirely to the same scale. The inclusion of 10 mini-figures means you can recreate most scenes from the films, even if getting Quirrel, but not Snape seems a bit odd. It's a little disappointing that there's only room for two of the four house banners to be hung up (though both are double-sided, so you can pick which ones you want to display), and it's not easy to reach inside the Hall once it's put together to get figures into it, but littler builders with smaller hands will have no problems.Overall, a fun set to build, and display. My only real complaint was that I wish it was bigger, and more complete version of the Hogwarts Castle, but I'm not a Lego fanatic, so I could have missed that, or maybe it's coming in the future?I gave this to my 8 year old grandchild! She loved it and spent hours of fun putting it together and playing with it.We got the wrong lego set by mistake. Accidentally got the Whomping Willow set instead of the Great Hall. Seller was super responsive and made it right quickly. I was very impressed by that! The actual set is incredible too—lots of fine details. My 12 year old daughter is loving it!Came in quickkyNot a hard lego to assemble.This is a pricey set, but there's a lot of value in it. We got it as a centerpiece birthday present and it was a big hit, as you can imagine.Minifigs, even generic ones, aren't cheap. The ten Potter-specific ones that come with this set add a lot of value. That's before you get to the fact that this works as both an advanced building set and as an interesting play setting. Lots of detail, bits and bobs, (sorting hat), and goofy accessories, (basilisk?), add a great deal to the play value and the overall appeal and value of the set.So, we were happy and G'son was happy. Mission accomplished.LEGO true to his name, good quality item.Took a good amount of time to complete, very enjoyable. Looks very good.Hogwarts Great Hall is one of my favourite Wizard World sets. It looks fantastic from both outside and inside. The Great Hall is highly detailed. There is plenty of room to play with the minifigures. Furthermore, the architectural design of the castle is absolutely beautiful and it includes several new details which could prove to be extremely useful.The minifigure selection is including a tremendous range of characters which are of a consistently high standard. I think there are certain areas of the castle which could be refined with a little more detail but this is still a great set. In addition The price is very reasonable and I would therefore highly recommend adding it to your Lego collections.Está genial éste set, viene de un excelente tamaño para que los niños se diviertan mucho, es principalmente parte del comedor del castillo pero vienen otras salas pero pequeñitas, me gustó en especial porque contiene a la mayoría de los personajes principales, ya para completar puedes comprar uno que otro set en específico si necesitas un personaje en especial, pero por lo pronto con éste ya tienes los que más valen la pena.Si eres fan de Harry Potter , este es el castillo de tus sueños. Trae muchos detalles como el sombrero seleccionador, el ave fenix, el basilisco, pequeñas escaleras que se mueven , el gran comedor, las banderas del equipo ganador etc. Simple y sencillamente lo ame.Lo unico que creo que le falta al castillo es el baño y la llorona Myrtle, pero no se puede tener todo en la vida. Lo que tiene el castillo es excelente y tiene un tamaño perfecto.

top_review: I originally bought an 8-pack of these to store out of season clothes & decor items. Fast forward 2 years & we were getting ready to move so I bought 10 more to pack & move all of our clothes, linens, etc. The movers were impressed with how easy it was to carry these, compared to boxes of clothes.I love how sturdy these bags are. None of the original 8 have ripped or been compromised in any way, despite being stored in a non-climate controlled storage unit for 2 years. They fit easily on our racks & the clear plastic pocket makes it convenient to drop a card/paper in describing the contents (pro tip: A 3x3 post-it note fits quite well). When not in use, they are a little cumbersome to get back into their original compact folded shape, but even a little puffy they take up far less room than boxes.We have one permanently set up as our family emergency "go bag" since it fits enough soft & lighter-weight items for our family of 5, plus 2 cats. We've used one to pack up & store common items we use for traveling & camping like extra extension cords, fans, ponchos, etc. It's so easy to just grab it & go. However, while I wouldn't necessarily be comfortable using it for a trip where we were flying, I have definitely used it for trips where we were driving (the bag also comes in handy as a dirty clothes hamper during these trips).As others have mentioned, these bags are much bigger than you are probably expecting & will hold an incredible amount of stuff. That being said, take caution not to over-pack.

title: Lodge Combo Cooker Cast Iron, 10.25", Black
description: It's a deep skillet, a fryer, a Dutch oven, and the lid converts to a shallow skillet or griddle. The Lodge Combo Cooker is a versatile piece of cast iron cookware that allows the preparation of almost any recipe. Great for kitchen and outdoor cooking.
top_review: VERY heavy. Lots of TLC required. Versatile. Multi-generational. Reasonably priced. Lodge seasoned CI-made in USA.First of all, for those of you who care about country of origin, rest assured that Lodge seasoned cast iron is made in the USA (the enameled Lodge cast iron however, is made in China).Before I delve into the review of this LCI, let me just warn my readers that CI is rather heavy! If you have arthritis or a weak arm and had, you may want to consider a lighter-weight cookware.Now on to the “meat” (pun intended) portions of this review…Cast iron is a forgiving but high maintenance mistress! She will forgive almost anything (even allowing her to rust!!!), but she does require a little TLC before, during, and after each use. The TLC she needs is:1. Before using: season CI1) Cast iron must be seasoned before any use; luckily, Lodge double seasons its cast iron so that customers may use the product right out of the box, but if you need to re-season the cast iron product, follow these steps:i) Scrub CI well in hot soapy water.ii) Dry thoroughly.iii) Spread a thin layer of oil (I like avocado oil, but vegetable or canola will suffice) over the CI (interior, exterior, handle, all parts).iv) Place CI upside down on a middle oven rack and turn on the oven and allow to heat to 550°. (PLEASE refrain from placing the CI into an already heated oven; the CI heat gradually in the oven as the oven works its way up to 550 degrees F)(1) ***NOTE: temperature depends on the oil being used to season (AO has a high smoking point, but VO and CO have lower smoking points; this means that if you are using VO or CO, you need to set the oven to 400 degrees instead of 550).v) Place foil on a lower rack to catch drips.vi) Once the oven temperature reaches 550 degrees, “bake” the CI for 50-90 minutes.vii) Turn off the oven and allow the CI to cool inside the oven.***Reminder: temperature depends on the oil being used to season (AO has a high smoking point, but VO and CO have lower smoking points; this means that if you are using VO or CO, you need to set the oven to 400 degrees instead of 550).2. During usage: use a “fatty food” the first time you use the CI implement.a. Personally, I love any excuse to fry bacon, so I always “break-in” my CI with bacon slices; however, there are many amongst you who are unable to partake in bacon for religious, moral and ethical, or environmental reasons. For those amongst you who cannot use bacon, cook a food that requires deep frying.b. Pre-heat the CI before using (every single time) or your food will stick and crumblei. NOTE: Although I ALWAYS pre-heat my CI for cooking, I rarely do so for cake-baking; for cake-baking I used a very liberal amount of my home-made pan release “goo” to fully coat the pan, and I pour the cake batter right into the pan; works every time!3. After using: wash and re-season (NO, not the detailed steps mentioned above)a. After using the CI, and while it is still hot, wash using scorching (wear heat resistant gloves as to not burn your hands) water and salt (refrain from using chemical cleaners)i. NEVER wash in a dishwasher (OMG)b. Dry completely and thoroughlyc. Spread a thin layer of oil over the CI (interior, exterior, handle, all parts) and place the CI on the stove top to heat for about 10 minutesd. Store CI in a moisture free environmenti. NEVER store food in CIii. NEVER store CI in fridge or freezerSo that is the TLC required for a CI pan or pot, but there are still several things to keep in mind:A. NOT everything should be cooked in cast iron!(1) Avoid cooking acidic foods in CI (yes, it is okay to finish the dish with a small squeeze of lemon (not when skillet is hot) or a few drops of vinegar, it is okay to add tomatoes and tomato paste to the dish you are cooking, but it is NEVER okay to stew tomato prolonged periods, deglaze with vinegar, or lemon juice to foods while they were still hot on the skillet)(2) Avoid (at least in the beginning when your cast iron is still getting TLC) sticky foods (fried eggs, omelets, pancakes, scrambled eggs, fried rice, crepes, etc.) as they will definitely stick to your CI; this is not to say that you will not eventually be able to fry eggs or make crepes on your CI, I do all the time, but you will need to have reused and reasoned you CI many times before it becomes fully non-stick.(3) Avoid cooking delicate fish (flounder, tilapia, etc.) In CI because the delicate fish will not tolerate the heat retained by the CI (an asset when searing steak) and will fall apart when flipped.(4) Avoid (particularly before your CI becomes super well-seasoned) using the same pan for savory and sweet as the CI does retain flavors; in other words, using the CI to bake a vanilla cake immediately the day after using it to make garlic chicken may make your vanilla a tad too garlicky!(5) Avoid using CI to cook foods that require lengthy periods of simmering, boiling, or steaming as the lengthy simmering, boiling, or steaming will strip your CI of its hard-earned seasoning.Are you still reading? If after reading the previous portions of this review, you are concerned about the TLC necessary to maintain CI, then I really recommend you consider other cookware options. (Caphlan non-stick is a viable alternative); if on the other hand, you are still reading, then you are not dissuaded from investing in CI cookware, and I am glad of that!There are numerous benefits to cooking and baking in CI:1) Cast iron is extremely sturdy and is very difficult to ruin. (If you do ruin a CI pan, you can restore and reclaim it!).2) Cast iron heats up evenly and retains heat incredibly well, which makes CI excellent for searing meat, baking corn bread, making pies, baking crusty bread, etc., and for keeping food warm as you serve it!3) Cast iron is healthy; yes, that is true! During the cooking process a trace amount of iron is absorbed into the foods, and when the foods are consumed by you, you are getting some iron into your system (a healthy by-product of CI cooking).4) Cast iron is quite versatile. You may use CI for almost everything (you make slow cook a lamb leg to perfect or make a three-layer birthday cake for your daughter in CI). Additionally, CI goes from cupboard, to stove-top, to oven, to camp-fire, and to dinner table! Talk about versatility!5) Cast iron is of heirloom status; it lasts for generations! I personally have a huge collection, and I plan to bequest my CI to my daughter (it shall be written in my will-not kidding).So, to re-cap:CI is a rather heavy type of cookware that offers great versatility, heats evenly, retains heat well, requires pre-seasoning and re-seasoning, and is multi-generational. And, of course, Lodge is an excellent CI brand. Lodge was founded in 1896 and is one of the very few remaining companies that still produce seasoned CI in the US (in the Lodge foundries in Tennessee). Lodge products are sturdy, versatile, heirloom-quality, and of course reasonably priced (as compared to the more expensive companies).I have been using CI (especially Lodge) for two and one-half decades (yes, ¼ of a century) now, and I will NEVER use anything else! A purchase of Lodge CI cookware and bakeware is a very sound investment indeed!**If you found this review of use, please “like” using the thumbs-up button below. Thank you.I've seen some reviews on this pan rated at 1-star that claim it's "not real cast iron" or that they have a "coating" when they see spots like the one I have pictured. These people don't seem to understand cast iron or the factory seasoning process.What's actually happening here is that when it's pre-seasoned at the factory, they hang the pan on hooks. Those spots are just where it was hanging during that process. It's not "damaged", it's just how it comes. If there are any cracks in the pan, then that is a different story. All you need to do is rub a bit of oil on the spots, heat, and go about your day. Within six moths of regular use, you won't even be able to find where the spots were. The second picture in my review is what the spot looked like after just one round of seasoning, and I haven't even cooked on it yet.I will say that Lodge could do a better job of packaging these pans for shipping. I received mine in a box with just a sheet of brown paper between the pot and lid, and no padding at all. Then again, this isn't delicate glass cookware, it's thick, heavy cast iron and is literally bulletproof.My cast iron skillets and cookware are my most priced. But you got to know how to treat them. I'm tired of reading reviews that complain about rust, educate yourself on how to use them, to not use soap when cleaning etc. After rinsing, I add some oil and let it sit on a hot plate, then wipe it off with a paper towel. Done!If you have rust spots, oil it and leave it in the oven for an hour. Check out youtube for more specifics. A bit cumbersome, I know but so well worth it!Had this set for 12 years. Our non-stick skillets come and go but this set is still around and works even better than new. We use the bottom part for deep frying and bread making (with the lid on). We use the lid/skillet section for great skillet corn bread and pan pizza. The seasoning is good enough to fry eggs and omelets without any sticking.It's nice to have a brand-new non-stick skillet for making that perfect French omelet, but this skillet will do it too. And it will out-live you if you take care of it. And even if you don't take care of it... It will still out-live you.If you mess up the seasoning (I won't deny I've messed up a skillet's seasoning way back when I was learning), it is a simple task to throw it in the oven with the self-cleaning cycle to burn off all that seasoning and start over again from scratch and get that pristine, like-new finish again. With a Teflon skillet... only thing to do is throw it in the trash.Over the years this set will grow on you just like a great classic car and will be your best friend.I bought these a couple of years ago and used a couple of times but it seemed like a little hard work. My reasoning is that food stuck quite easily even though I followed the seasoning instructions from the Lodge web site, but on the skillet, things stuck very easily and on the large pot, it seemed to rust a bit through the black seasoning and things stick easily. So they were put away in the cupboard.Since that time I have been to shops and noticed that the more expensive brands like Staub and Le Crueset, have a lot smoother surface to begin with. Designed for little hands to hold, our snacking containers fit in cupholders, diaper bags, backpacks and more—making them an awesome food storage choice for daycare, school, and on-the-go airplane or car travel. So if you want healthy snacking to be simple (and loads of fun), don’t miss these containers!

Very neat! Super easy to setup and put wherever you want. Great value for money!This product works as advertised and meets all of our needs. Easy to install. NOTE: Other than the initial "doorbell chime" most of the other settings are musical with a XMAS carol themes for most of them, not exactly what we thought they would be. We settled for the standard doorbell chime. Note: to manufacturer/Amazon, provide some way of allowing a customer to sample the chimes included prior to purchase. Will update this review in 12 months.I could never hear my doorbell. This works so well because the receiver has different ringtones and a volume control. It even has a little blue light that comes on when someone rings it. I have one receiver in the dining room and one in my bedroom. Now, I never miss a visitor or delivery. No batteries needed as it somehow uses friction to power the bell. You just plug in the receivers, adjust the ringtone and volume and that's it. Wow. I have all three colors (black, blue, red), but sometimes I like to color-code my notes, and it would be helpful to have at least the basic rainbow of colors (except yellow - that's pretty useless in terms of writing and notes). I know Pilot offers this in their gel pens, but I prefer the ink and glide of the Easy Touch pens, there are no worries about smudging or bleed-through with these. I do have multicolor sets of fine point felt-tip or journaling-type pens that are okay, but I really prefer how these write, so I mostly use those to highlight or accent something, when necessary.I did have an issue with two boxes in a "business" order that were packaged with heavy-duty cleaner that leaked - it seems like the cleaner messed up the ink flow. description: Product Description ESSENTIAL TRAVEL TOOL Whether you're traveling around the world or working around the house, the 3.6" Tinker prepares you for any situation. SHARPENING To re-sharpen your knife, use a whetstone at an angle of 15°– 20°. This will result in a cutting angle of 30°– 40°. If sharpening on a grinding wheel, always cool with plenty of water to avoid excessive temperatures and the resulting damages that may occur. HISTORY & HERITAGE In 1884, Master Cutler Karl Elsener opened a cutlery shop in Ibach, Switzerland. There, he and his cutlers’ union produced the finest steel cutlery, finished with the now-famous proprietary edge preferred globally by professionals and home cooks. Karl supplied the Swiss Army with its standard issue Soldier’s Knife and Officer’s Knife. After the death of his mother, and with the advent of stainless steel, Karl changed the name of the company to Victorinox. It is from those humble beginnings that a worldwide icon was born. Today, Victorinox is still owned and operated by the Elsener family, and both the company and family still resides in the small village of Ibach, Switzerland. This Swiss Army knife features; large and small blades, can and bottle openers, large and small screwdrivers, Phillips screwdriver, wire stripper, and reamer with sewing eye. top_review: This is a quality knife in my book but I figured it was made in China but evidently it's not. On the large blade it states "Victorinox Swiss made stainless" and on the other side "Officier Suisse." Anyway, regardless of where it's made this is a solid knife. This knife fits the bill for an everyday carry knife and that's exactly what I do. It slips easily in the pocket and has most of the things that you'd need...minus the scissors.It is small. Has just enough blades to fix minor problems. My last one lasted 15 years before one of the blades broke. This one is the exact same quality.As soon as I picked up this particular knife I was sure. Thin, light, short, but not too short to end up with too short knives, or tools.I’ve only had this particular knife for a few months, but so far I’ve been completely satisfied with the choice of tools. Sure there are more tools that I could use, this is not my first Swiss Army knife, I have quite a few, including one of the larger ones with lots of tools. Still, when you boil it down, certain tools get used more than others. Corkscrews and wood saws are rarely used everyday for me at least. Scissors too, though often used, are just too small for a sturdy implementation. Far better to have a good sharp knife, or two really, in this case a smaller one that works for higher leverage uses, box cutting, or any use that benefits a smaller blade to prevent inadvertent cuts. The longer knife shines for easy cutting of larger items, and doubles for a food knife.As a comparison, I have a much smaller multi-tool. It is smaller that this knife by half, and it has more tools, but it fails In the sturdy catagory, the single knife is just too small, with a tiny spine, and a one side taper that makes sharpening difficult. That life sits in my knife drawer, waiting with all the others to find it’s use.The color, black, is better for discrete pocket use. I like the red color, but for everyday pocket use, black is better.Could there be more tools that would fit in this exactly right pocket size? Sure, the pressurized pen comes to mind. It has the toothpick and the tweezers that find quite a bit of daily use. Another would be the magnifier, but not if the width is larger.With the Swiss sharpener tool used to give these blades a finish at the factory, the knives remain almos razor sharp, yet much sturdier.Also, if it wouldn’t change the knife dimensions, a locking blade would be welcomed. Yet strangely I don’t miss the lock as much as I thought I would, pretty every use I’ve tasked these knife blades for, the lock wouldn’t have mattered.If you need a larger knife, you would probably utilize a knife belt holster.Nothing wrong with this, but it doesn’t fit within the pocket cary CarryAt this point, this knife is the currently designated “Everyday Pocket Carry”.I have owned many Swiss Army Knives over the last 50 years or more. First knife I ever bought was one of these but this is my favorite size for EDC because it has what I need and nothing more. I hate the ones with a cork screw instead of a philips and I don't need to carry scissors all day, a sharp knife will cut things just fine for me and if I need scissors, I have them on my Leatherman that I keep in my briefcase. I carried the Cadet of the last 5 years, but Nutin Fancy is wrong about that one, it's just not got enough tools on there to make it worth pocket space. The smaller SA knives are too small to do much, I like the size of the screw drivers on this tinker the best but the bigger SA knives take up too much space for things I never really use. This is the American version of the SA knife, tools Americans need and use. I carry this mostly for the tools on it besides the knives because I always carry a 4 in. lock blade of my choice of that day, I have many to pick from. I like having this knife always with me as a back up incase I forget the real knife. This is not expensive so it makes sense to give it a try for a few months, I think you'll love this sweat spot of SA knives.I want to love this knife so much. It’s a perfect size with a perfect blend of tools. Slides into your pocket and you forget about it.But the quality is second rate. This is my second Victorinox Tinker, and I’ve ended up returning them both. After forgetting both knives in my pocket and running them through the dryer, the plastic scales have popped off. I’m guessing this is because the heat of the dryer softened the glue.Technically, this is my fault. I shouldn’t wash and dry my knife with my clothes. But the entire point of a value knife is that you CAN forget about it in your pocket, and it’s okay. I’ve owned so many inexpensive knives and washed and dried them, left them dirty, left them in the bed of the truck, ect, and they’ve held up.No so the Tinker. I used both knives very gently (other than the dryer) and both have become heavily scratched very easily. Plus the weak glue problem.I’m going to try a Pioneer Alox (no plastic grips) and hopefully find a more robust knife. I also own a Victorinox Locksmith and have been very pleased. So maybe the $30 Tinker is just a cheaper model.I wish there was a Tinker Alox. Because it really is the perfect design. Just not very durable.Totally pleased with this knife. Wanted a handy good quality pocket knife and this really does the trick. Highly recommend and getting alot of use out it. Will admit I am one of those who likes to carry a pocket knife 'everywhere' I go so this works just great for that purpose.Any genuine Swiss Army Knife is a nice knife. My Tinker with black scales is no different. The quality is what you'd expect. Excellent steel on the tools. The blades are nice and sharp out of the box. All the hinges have that same satisfying snap that Swiss Army Knives are known for.The Tinker is a Spartan with a Phillips screwdriver instead of a corkscrew. This is a great substitution in my opinion. The corkscrew can be useful for picking a knot say, or holding a mini screwdriver. But I've never actually needed a corkscrew for a cork...I find myself often using the screwdriver though. So that's great.Also the Tinker/Spartans are just two layer knives, which makes them nice and slim in the pocket. Perfect for an Every Day Carry (EDC).The black scales look really nice, though they do show finger prints. I enjoy the change from the classic red though.To sum up, this knife is a great entry in the Swiss Army lineup. And it has all the build quality you'd expect from Victorinox.Excellent pocket knife. It's in my pocket everyday. The blades come razor sharp, the can opener works well, the awl is great for making holes in leather, you can really tighten screws with the phillips head screwdriver and the bottle opener doesn't tear the side of the cap like other small can openers.Great slim SAK to carry in your pocket for everyday. Black scales look great, product arrived in perfect condition.Bought it discounted. Always liked Victorinox products. Need one with the philips screwdriver.El producto tiene la calidad de la marca Victorinox y está en un precio muy adecuado.La navaja es obligada para la gente que hace salidas de campo.La recomiendo mucho por el precio.

title: Aprilaire 216 Replacement Furnace Air Filter for Aprilaire Whole Home Air Purifiers, MERV 16, Allergy, Asthma, & Virus Furnace Filter (Pack of 1)
description: The air in your home has the potential to impact the health and wellness of you and your family. With Aprilaire you have the power to use your whole-home air cleaner to remove allergy and asthma triggers from the air circulating through your HVAC system to help create a cleaner and healthier home environment during allergy season and all year long. The Aprilaire 216 Allergy, Asthma, & Virus Air Filter captures up to 96% of virus-size airborne particles including tobacco smoke and smog, and up to 99% of airborne allergy and asthma triggers including dust, pollen, mold spores, bacteria, pet dander, and dust mites by circulating the air in your home through the MERV 16 filter. For help with allergy and asthma triggers during allergy season and beyond, trust the Aprilaire 216 Allergy, Asthma, & Virus Air Filter. Genuine Aprilaire filters are specifically engineered to work with your Aprilaire air cleaner. They are effective for 6-12 months compared to the traditional 1-3 month filter, saving you time and money. Our 4-inch filters provide more filter surface area for harmful particles to be captured compared to the traditional 1-inch filters. Aprilaire's patented self-seal technology assures no air will pass by unfiltered, keeping your home clean and HVAC system operating at peak performance. Note: MERV is a scale used to measure the effectiveness of air filters. Higher number values translate to more effective filtration. Choose the Aprilaire Filter with the MERV rating that fits the needs of your family and home. *Performance tested to ASHRAE 52.2 Standard, minimum efficiency reporting value – MERV 16
categories: ["Tools & Home Improvement","Building Supplies","HVAC","Furnace Parts & Accessories","Furnace Filters"]
top_review: Aprilaire offers four filter versions for my particular home HVAC system. I have now purchased and am in the process of using (for comparison) three of the four styles available (the two 213 rated versions, and the 216), two ordered from Amazon (the 213CBN and 216). (My own home had the model 210 originally installed. My HVAC service company installed the 213 model when service was most recently performed, and I have now decided to upgrade to the 213CBN and 216 models and have purchased them from Amazon).As stated above my personal choice is to use either the 213CBN, or the 216 version. The 216 has the ability to remove significantly more particles of all sizes down to 0.3 μm. The 213CBN includes activated carbon filter material for better removal of odors and VOCs. Both are quite a bit more expensive than either the 210 or 213, and have potentially shorter life (6 mo vs 12 mo). I feel that the added cost is well worthwhile - my home requires only one of these filters, and if I have to replace them somewhat more frequently in order to ensure the best possible filtration for air in my home, I consider that to be money well spent.The key difference between these filters from my point of view is this - any of the filters rated at MERV 13 or greater is going to provide a very high level of filtration, and the MERV 16 rated filter is really superior filtration. According to the EPA paper I reference below, anything above MERV 16 is considered to be a HEPA filter. Residential filters are only required to provide an efficiency of MERV 6 or greater (per ANSI/ASHRAE Standard 62.2-2007).The filters that I received from purchasing here on Amazon were authentic OEM Aprilaire products in the proper packaging. I purchased from Amazon itself, not one of the third party sellers.Below are more details of the various models available, to help explain the differences:- 210 Clean Air Filter for Aprilaire Whole-Home Air Purifiers, MERV 11, For Dust--- least expensive (MSRP 52.99)--- described by Aprilaire as effective for removing airborne particles including dust, pollen, mold spores, bacteria, and pet dander--- rated MERV 11--- filter life stated by Aprilaire as 'up to 12 months'--- MERV 9-12 typical applications** described as: "Superior residential, Better commercial buildings, Hospital laboratories"--- MERV 11 particle removal efficiency is not rated for particle sizes 0.3 to 1 μm, 65-80% for 1 to 3 μm, >85% for 3 to 10 μm (see reference below for source of this information)- 213 Healthy Home Air Filter for Aprilaire Whole-Home Air Purifiers, MERV 13, for Most Common Allergens--- slightly more expensive (MSRP 59.99)--- described by Aprilaire as effective for removing common airborne allergens including dust, pollen, mold spores, bacteria, pet dander and dust mites--- rated MERV 13--- filter life stated by Aprilaire as 'up to 12 months'--- MERV 13-16 typical applications include: "Superior commercial buildings, Hospital inpatient care, General surgery"--- MERV 13 particle removal efficiency is <75% for particle sizes 0.3 to 1 μm, > 90% for 1 to 10 μm (see reference below for source of this information)- 213CBN Odor Reduction Air Filter for Aprilaire Whole-Home Air Purifiers, MERV 13, for Odors and Most Common Allergens--- most expensive (MSRP 94.99)--- described by Aprilaire as effective for removing common airborne allergens + odors, including dust, pollen, mold spores, bacteria, pet dander, dust mites, pet and cooking odors, and VOCs--- rated MERV 13 (plus activated Carbon for odor and VOC reduction)--- filter life stated by Aprilaire as 'up to 6 months'--- MERV 13-16 typical applications include: "Superior commercial buildings, Hospital inpatient care, General surgery"--- MERV 13 particle removal efficiency is <75% for particle sizes 0.3 to 1 μm, > 90% for 1 to 10 μm (see reference below for source of this information)- 216 Allergy and Asthma Air Filter for Aprilaire Whole-Home Air Purifiers, MERV 16, for Allergy and Asthma Triggers--- most expensive (MSRP 94.99)--- described by Aprilaire as effective for removing up to 99% of allergy and asthma triggers, including dust, pollen, mold spores, bacteria, pet dander, dust mites, viruses, and the airborne particulates associated with tobacco smoke and smog--- rated MERV 16--- filter life stated by Aprilaire as 'up to 6 months'--- MERV 13-16 typical applications include: "Superior commercial buildings, Hospital inpatient care, General surgery"--- MERV 16 particle removal efficiency is > 95% for particle sizes 0.3 to 10 μm (see reference below for source of this information)** Ref: US EPA publication EPA 402-F-09-002, revised August 2009, "Residential Air Cleaners, second edition, A Summary of Available Information"(VOC = volatile organic compounds, organic chemicals such as formaldehyde that are released from paint and plastics into the air)They fit well and they dont smell like so many other filters sold these days. I have re purchased another set because of the quality.Buying from Amazon allows me to try different filter styles such as Standard filter, Dust filters,etcPerfect fit and less expensive than at HVAC supplier.Recently upgraded to an Aprilaire air cleaner housing for my HVAC. The design of this is superb for ensuring a tighter seal so that the filter medium can actually catch more air contaminants to more closely match the listed filter rating. The design is basically an accordion style folding filter medium with two plastic ends that you extend and slide on to a couple of rails in the air cleaner housing to ensure a perfect fit every time. Ease of replacement makes it quick and painless.Super easy install and does a great job cleaning up the air especially with 3 dogs in the houseIn short these filters (216) work well - trapping anything that goes through your system bigger than a few microns (pollen, cat hair, etc). Consider these important points Aprilaire may not tell you about the Aprilaire 216 modelI don't see anyone discussing the last two hereAprilaire 216 Specific problems1. Problem: Clogging. Replace these often. Mine is 70% clogged after six weeks of Spring/Summer and totally clogged after twelve.2. Problem: Water condensation. Humid outside? A/C running all the time in that Summer heat wave? Look out for water buildup on the wall of the coil section of your unit (above the flame usually). My HVAC technician was standing there and pointed out water droplets forming up on the surface of my new Carrier central air system where the coil is located. Water was slowly dripping. "That water buildup is not normal. It is caused by that filter. It is not letting air pass by the coils at a rate the unit is designed for" . It's harmless but be aware". I put a towel down.3. Problem? Furnace fire hazard. When you inevitably forget to change the 216 filter it will clog up to a dangerous level. In Winter, when the furnace is running longer, the air can't get through the heat exchanger fast enough. Too much heat can lead to a house fire. Lookup the anatomy of a forced air furnace. One of the components is the "heat exchanger". The flames push their heat into the heat exchanger. The exchanger gets extremely hot. The only reason it doesn't start a dangerous situation (like a fire) is the giant blower nearby "forces" the air throughout your home. With that 216 filter, inevitably neglected and clogged, you might as well not have a fan. This alone is probably why my HVAC manual does not mention the Apriiaire 216 even though it is designed to accept this series.I use the Aprilaire 216 filter in the Spring and Summer (putting up with the water buildup)We like itThese are great filters - take almost all allergens out of the air - well worth the $.They arrive on time as well.

I use them for my art business - i am very particular with getting strong colour in my designs and these pencil crayons deliver results that met my expectations.They blend well after a few layers and can take a build up of colour. The finish is smooth (if blended) or a grainy finish if used in few layers (so works really nicely over the top of watercolour or promarkers to give a bit of texture).My one piece of advice is you shouldn’t attempt to blend with other types of pencil crayon...I've never used these waxy types of crayon before and didn’t realise how different they are to ‘standard’ pencil crayons. I use the full size Derwent SuperPoint handcrank sharpener, and it works great. Absolutely love the creaminess and blendability of these pencils. I liked the Prismacolor Premiers so well, that once I felt sure that I wasn’t going to have an issue sharpening them, I bought the 72 pack, too.Really liked these at first, blends well, layers great, good pigment... but why make such good cores n make rubbish outers for them. Over half have now got splits all the way down the length of the pencil and I’ve had to tightly tape them so I can sharpen and use them. They were going to be my ‘only buy’ colour pencils.... but I think I’ll work more with my derwent Inktense ... they seem better overall.

description: Product Description GUND is proud to introduce Philbin, one of our most popular character bears, in a 12” and 18” seated teddy bear format, in creamy vanilla beige and chocolate brown hues. Philbin features a classic design with oversized paws, featuring cute paw pad accents, and a curious expression that’s impossible not to love! Building upon our award-winning and beloved plush designs, we continue to practice innovation by constantly developing new original and licensed designs to appeal to the next generation of customers. To that end, each one of our plush toys is constructed with pride from premium materials for unparalleled softness and sustained huggability through the years. From established classic favorites to brand-new modern pals, there’s a GUND teddy bear plush for everyone! top_review: TL;DR version:Gund bears and stuffed animals have been around since I was a preteen so I wanted to find Gund teddy bears for two expected great-grands, one boy and one girl.  I looked at all the Gund bears, read many reviews on each, and narrowed it down to Slumbers and Philbin.  I decided on one of each and I'm delighted with both of them!  Super soft, appear to be well made, and oh so huggable!Comparisons below and in the attached photo.Because I had already bought a soft cloth "first doll" for the expected girl, the first bear I looked for was for the expected boy.  I'm fascinated by grizzly bears and wanted a (sweet) bear with that look for him.Slumbers seemed to fit that bill.  One review said that Slumbers isn't as weighted as Philbin and although only an inch shorter than the larger (18" version) Philbin, Slumbers looked a good bit smaller because of Philbin's larger head.  I ordered Slumbers and loved him so much I immediately ordered another for myself, LOL.  I love his round fat tummy and big bear paws.After a few days of loving these bears I decided the girl must also get one at her baby shower, too, along with the soft doll (both are also getting small white fluffy lambs, but oh well!), but I wanted a different style for her and maybe a lighter color.  Philbin is available in light and dark fur in two sizes.  I was afraid the larger 18" Philbin would be too big and maybe heavier so I decided on the 12" beige Philbin.  He arrived today and is also perfect!Both look just like the photos on their product pages and both are adorable.  Both will easily sit unsupported, although I can't detect that either is weighted.  Both are lightweight.  Both's legs will hang down when picked up.  (I don't understand the review that said Slumbers is in a permanent sitting position; he isn't.)  Both are very, very soft, have sweet faces, and are totally lovable and huggable.  Both came sealed in a Gund plastic bag with an attached Gund tag and sewn-in label.  The website says surface washable only, but several reviews mention gently washing and air drying with no harm.Slumbers is a 17" bear (about 11" when seated), and I got the 12" Philbin (9" when seated).  Slumbers has a bigger body/tummy and smaller head and has a sweet papa bear look.  Philbin has a proportionally larger head and smaller body and he has a sweet, more whimsical look.  Philbin's front paws are proportionally larger.  I love the big bear paws on their hind legs and both have those.  Very pleased with these bears, and any of the others would probably be just as adorable.  They also seem to be a good value for the brand and quality at the price I paid (about $24 for each.)  However, the prices vary greatly from day to day, sometimes even doubling.These are great teddy bears for the young or old and I hope the babies will love them.Edit to add:  Their fur is not scraggly-looking!  No idea why the photo looks that way.  They are both good-looking bears.

top_review: I stumbled upon the TRX bands while searching for something else, and I’m very glad I purchased them.  The bands work great, and our whole family is now using them in our exercise room (there's a lot of expensive equipment in there collecting dust while we use the TRX bands now).I installed the bands in the ceiling using this TRX X-mount and it has worked perfect.  For me, mounting these on the ceiling was much much better than attaching them to the top of a door.  To me, it wouldn’t be worth it if I had to mount it on top of a door.  The main exercise I wanted to do with these was inverted rows, and those require that you lay flat on the ground almost directly under the ceiling mount.  So if I had mounted it on at the top of a door, then inverted rows wouldn’t have been possible (nowhere to put your feet / extend your legs).This mount easily bolted in to the ceiling joist in our exercise room (the joist was 1.5 inches wide and I used a stud finder to ensure I drilled into the middle of it for maximum stability).  The mount is very very secure … doesn't move or sway at all.One suggestion – make sure you download the TRX Accessory X-Mount installation instructions.  I just double checked, and for whatever reason the detailed instructions don’t seem to have come in the box?  I found the online installation instructions by accident when searching online to find out what size drill bit to use to drill the pilot holes in the ceiling.The install instructions were especially helpful because they clarified the exact workout space I needed to take full advantage of the bands.  The original TRX box said you needed a workout space of 8 ft deep by 6 ft wide, and I just assumed the 8 feet was straight back from where you mount them on the ceiling.  But that’s not the case.  The X-mount install instructions clarify that the recommended workout distance is 5 ft back from the ceiling mount, while leaving 3 ft in front of you (5 + 3 = 8 ft).  Bottom line – For me, mounting on the ceiling was definitely the way to go.  Otherwise, I wouldn’t have been able to do certain exercises (included the inverted rows that I bought the bands for in the first place).  I also moved some other equipment around to make sure the workout space for these was the recommended width of 6 ft wide (3 ft on each side).  Having the full 8 ft X 6 ft space available to work out in makes a big difference, and the ceiling mount is a ton better than a door.Very happy with this X-mount.  Very easy to install and it has worked perfectly.  Took less than 30 min to install (after I found the instructions :)

description: If you're looking for tip-top protection for your documents, look no further than these Secure Top™ Sheet Protectors. Each plastic sheet protector features a convenient top flap that secures the contents within, so you can store papers in nonstandard sizes with confidence knowing your important document won't accidentally slip out of its protective sleeve. These heavyweight sheet protectors are designed to both protect your papers and show them off impressively with diamond-clear material that delivers a crisp view of your documents, scrapbooking pages, recipes and more. Each protector holds sheets up to 8.5" x 11" and is made from acid-free and archival safe polypropylene that won't lift print. Loading papers into the top-loading heavy duty sheet protectors is fast and easy, and a reinforced binding edge fortifies the protectors to prevent tearing. You can even use your clear plastic page protectors for 3 ring binders as a dry erase board. Jot down notes, check off items on your list, create practice lessons for kids or cross out tasks on your schedule by writing directly on the clear sheet protector with dry erase markers. When done, simply wipe the page protectors clean and reuse again and again. Give your frequently used documents, reports, recipes, photos and other important items the long-term protection and preservation they deserve with this pack of 25 diamond clear sheet protectors for 3 ring binders.

top_review: I have had this speaker for a little over a year now and i use it EVERVY DAY! It is a great bang for your buck. There are so many great color options to choose from. I rarely have to charge this thing and even when I do I don’t charge it for a while and it still gives me so many hours of listening time. It is so easy to clip onto my backpack or just clip it onto anything and it’s good to go. I take it to the pool and when it gets wet, who cares it’s water proof! It’s also a great shower speaker. Also it’s very easy to connect to your phone and once it connects for the first time as long as no one else connects to it all you have to do is turn it on and it’s connected! If you are looking for a sturdy, stylish, and portable speaker this is an amazing choice for you!

top_review: Awesome design, durable material, organized, good fit, and conservative.I am a working stagehand/audio/lighting/video/tv/film guy in NYC, so I am all over the place all the time, and a lot of times (most of the time really), I have to carry all my tools with me for a variety of jobs while staying 100% mobile and as compact as possible because I never know what I'm going to run into, and I ride trains everywhere. I could be on a TV shoot one day, then move to a theatrical lighting gig, and after that maybe ill be sent on an audio system permanent install job with zero turnaround time in between. This bag has performed phenomenally. Total load out sometimes 20-30 pounds and it doesn't suck as much as you'd think due to the yoke strap. I wasn't sure if the 12 pack would work for me, but it totally does. It is much deeper than I thought it would be. It isn't too small or too big. I researched tactical bags to death before I bought this one so do yourself a favor and just stop here. After I bought this and had it out at work, three other guys ordered the same bag within the last couple months - no joke. Within 15 minutes after I set it down the first day I had it, my production manager got on the radio and was like "where did you get this bag?"This thing is almost totally covered in MOLLE web. I have some Grimlocs For those of you out there searching for an alternative to the $300 backpack + $90 ruck plate from the "big brand" - this is your answer! The 5.11 RUSH12 backpack perfectly fits the Titan 20 lb. ruck plate (found here on Amazon) in the back hydration pocket - so no need to worry about it flopping around in a backpack's main/large compartment. I just wrapped it up in an old t-shirt to keep it as snug as possible, and to keep the rough-ish finish of the plate from abrading the inside of the pack. The Titan 30 lb. ruck plate should also fit in the hydration pocket, as the internal dimensions of the pocket are 17" tall x 11" wide, and the plate is 14.5" tall x 8.75" wide. The Titan 45 lb. ruck plate is 15" tall x 9.5" wide, so that should be fine too.The backpack itself seems plenty "tough" for this job - 1050D nylon, wide/sturdy/comfortable straps, heavy duty zippers, etc. Tons of MOLLE all over it for pouches, water bottle holders, etc. if you're into that. It's also very nice that is has the attachment points for a 1.5" waist belt (sold separately from the pack), as that will really help keep your ruck in place and comfortable. I bought the Fire Force waist belt here on Amazon, as they have all the military/tacti-cool colors to (mostly) match all the colors in which the RUSH12 is available.There was ZERO chance I was paying $175-295 for a rucking pack from the "big brand" - 5.11 RUSH packs are very well reviewed, made of similarly tough materials, fit the Titan ruck plates perfectly, and are well-suited for "fitness" rucking. 5.11 RUSH packs are not, however, made in the USA, which is probably part of the reason why the price points are so different from the "big brand".The Titan ruck plates are a great product too - my review for those are on that product page. The main message is - for $152, you can be "all in" to get started rucking for fitness, and that includes the $12 waist belt mentioned above. To recap - $100 for the 5.11 RUSH12, $40 for a Titan 20 lb. plate, and $12 for the Fire Force waist belt (buy a 1.5" for the RUSH packs). This is compared to $260 to $390 just to get started with the same setup from the "big brand"!My first ruck with the setup last night was great - 3 miles at a rather quick pace, pack felt very stable and secure. My wife rucked 3 miles with it this morning as well, and no complaints.Good day packAbsolutely one of the best purchases I’ve ever made! I have had this bag for almost ten years.It has been it the wet woods, up and down mountains and in the sandiest places I’ve been. It says rush 12, but, I have used this bag in the field for 48. I’m not saying that’s what it was designed to do but it held up. I now use it as an EDC. If you are looking to get a do everything and go anywhere bag; this is it. It is worth the money!They are tons of reviews here saying great organisation and quality, which I agree with, and won't repeat.It was a lot smaller than I expect in terms of bag height, it doesnt cover much of your back, and sticks out quite a lot instead of traveling down. This results in back pain when the bag is fully filled.I found a youtube review saying the exact same thing, that when you do pack it with heavier stuff it will give you lower back pain because of the space/weight distribution on your upper back.What made my bag heavy? 800ml water bottle, 500ml coffee flask, 13 inch laptop, headphones, and some accessories/maybe food. So definitely not enough to warrant backpain in a normal backpack.I bought the rush 24 instead which I have found to be miles better. Perfect bag for me. 10 out of 5 stars. I prefer the extra organisational pockets, and it is also so much more comfortable and ergonomic. I've never loved a bag like I love that bag.I unfortunately waited too long before I realised it was the bag was giving me serious back pain, so I wasn't able to return it. Its comfortable when light, but I dont find myself using it often, I just go for the rush 24 instead. So it has been wasted money for me.When I'm going out for leisure and only need to take some accessories and medication, maybe headphones, I use the rush 12, but for that purpose it is actually often a bit too big, and my girlfriend often comments "why do you have such a big bag?" which I dont mind, but I wish I got the MOAB instead to use it as a day bag, as the rush 12 can be a bit too big to bring to a restaurant or a bar.Reviews say you also have to keep the MOAB light because of ergonomics, but since this is also the case for the rush 12, I think I would have benefitted more from the added functionality of being easily able to swing it around for easy access.Edit: over the next few months I decided to lower the amount of things I carried day to day in my backpack, by having a locker at uni and just carrying essentials with me. by using the rush 12 as a low weight backpack it was amazing, and very comfortable. You can also tighten the straps and then its also a great looking compact backpack. It became my daily bag again and I was very happy with its performance as a low weight easy backpack. So I will change my review from 3 to 5 star, however its important to acknowledge what you're going to be using the backpack before and to gauge your expectations for that.Pondré la nota discordante en este recopilatorio de alabanzas a 5.11. En las fotos que adjunto se puede apreciar como la parte externa está intacta y como se ve que dentro un surco recorre toda la espuma de lado a lado. La mochila ya venía con eso cuando la compré y no le di importancia, sin embargo creo que el defecto o tara ha ido a más a lo largo del tiempo. top_review: Ok, while they are not super sheer, I like that about them because the color pops! The only ones I have an issue with when it comes to highlighting are the regular blue and dark purple. It's not that you can't see through them, but they are a tad too dark to be highlighters. Other than that, they're like my highlighter go-to! I am in school, so I highlight A LOT, and they lasted about 2 months with VERY heavy usage. I love that you can see how much ink is in them, so it's easy to know when to re-order. Highly recommend!I love that this has so many shades, and that is part of why I bought them. I don't feel like all of the colors are as sheer as I would prefer when a student is taking pictures to turn in or prove completion of work.I love these highlighters. They're good quality, low-bleed on 28lb paper, long-lasting, and perfect for color-coding planner and journal entries if you're a fan of personal growth techniques that advocate separating your life activities and goals into color-coded categories to develop better life balance and self-awareness. They're also a perfect color match to "Astrobright" colored papers. I use the latter to print out planner pages on which I list my goals and future plans by life area, and these pens to highlight entries in my planner and hourly diary to see how I'm actually spending my time day-to-day.I had a 4 pack that I loved and when I had used them all up, I was thrilled to find this larger variety of colors! There a 2 of the colors that are a tad darker than I prefer, but I just use them for other things.I have been using these highlighters for years. I have replaced them about 3 or 4 times now, but this time, I was disappointed to discover they no longer come with the plastic sleeve. I just ended up keeping the sleeve from my previous set. But why I wonder why Sharpie did away with this? I have included a pic as reference. The ones with black are the old set.This is a great package deal. There are enough colors to color code notes in important document or books. I use them in my file cabinet as well. My niece used them in her coloring book. They didn’t bleed through at all. Caps stay secure. The barrel is easy to hold even for arthritic hands.0Best highlighters ever!!Perfect addition for a classroom gift basket for my friendBest highlighter pens, great price and superb service.I never have enough highlighters - I don't know where they go but they are either missing or dried out when I need one. I finally bit the bullet and bought this 12 pack and am not drowning in highlighters.1. The clear bodies show you how much highlighter juice is left. No more dried out/dead highlighters2. Sharpie quality caps. They snap on securely - maybe this will help them not dry out?3. Fairly fine tip - if you're highlighting huge swaths maybe not the best, but for fine work they work well. Tip is a fine chisel so easy to write with or make super fine underlines too4. No bleed through - at least in normal use they don't soak through the page4. Only drawback is the ink does cause a bit of smudging in underlying writing (in my experience used on gel-ink notes)Overall these are quality highlighters, just wish they didn't smear things as much.Here’s my overly detailed review. I find these use a lot of ink while writing and bleed through the page even on a quick streak. The design of the markers is not as advertised as well, they don’t have the clear body with ink level lines, just black, which I found disappointing as I bought these partly for how they look. More so, I found the yellow to be not as bright as other sharpie highlighters I own, the orange and light pink were good highlighting colors, but the rest were dark and unevenly highlighted on typical paper as they soaked though in spots creating a patchy color. They didn’t instantly dry as other highlighters do, but were still quick to dry. I did find the water based formula was better for highlighting rollerball pen ink as it didn’t smear. Overall I have to say I’m a little disappointedFive stars for the product...Colours are awesome, can also be used as marker. So I will used it for writing titles and headers. Loved these. Will definitely buy again.Four stars because the price tag was removed two times then the latest one was pasted.These are excellent highlighters that don’t bleed or smudge. Most highlighters bleed through thin pages and of note these do not bleed through thin Bible pages, the best I have seen or used. A little more expensive but so worth the cost.
