top_review: I bought these bins for my local Mosque as our community is trying to increase our efforts to recycle, reduce waste, etc... We had nothing but trash cans before so I purchased 4 of these to disperse throughout our building.  So far they have been sturdy enough and durable enough.  We've not had them very long so I'm not sure how well they will hold up over time.  They do say their are commercial products so I'm hoping they will be as sturdy and durable as they claim.  The size is nice it's tall and slim so it can fit in many places but unfortunately the recycling symbol is only on the side.  So when it's up against our other bins with the narrow side out many people don't see the symbol.  If we turn it on it's side so that the long side is out with the symbol visible then it takes up a lot more unnecessary space.I only purchased the bins (we have limited funds and recycling bins have fallen towards the bottom of the list of necessities for many years) but as soon as more funds are available I want to purchase the covers which make it clear that bottles should go in the bins.  Maybe it's just our Muslim community but people just do not listen (despite signs right over the bin about what you can and cannot throw in it) to what we say about putting recycling in the bins.  Every day I find garbage in the bins (which we have to sort out) and recycling in the garbage.  So if you can I highly recommend getting the appropriate lids (their almost the same price as the bins which I think is ridiculous) so that it makes it even more painfully obvious for the lazy to know what goes in the bin and makes it more difficult to put things that don't belong in them.I really believe that the recycling symbol should be on all sides but at a minimum one large and one small side so that it's obvious no matter which way it's used.  The price on this bin is better than I found on similar bins locally by about $15 but I still feel the price was too high.  $35 seems high for a trash bin.  A regualar bin could be purchased for much less and had I found a blue one I might have just spray painted or put a vinyl decal on the bins to make them recycling bins.  Unfortunate I did not find any bright blue trash bins at that time.They feature a cinch system that's supposed to make it easy to hold the bag in place but nobody ever seems to take advantage of it even after I pointed it out.  I guess old habits die hard so I'm not holding out any hope of our cleaning crew making use of the feature but it seemed to work well enough when I tried it.I'm not sure how helpful the vent channels are... the bag didn't get stuck but the we haven't had much problem with that, perhaps because our recycling is generally filled with bottles and other lightweight trash items that it doesn't create as much of a suction.

I purchased two to use for art supplies and found them to be extremely functional. The trays are steep-sided so even my taller bottles of paints and mediums aren't in danger of falling out when I am moving the cart. The trays are sturdy plastic with vent holes for air circulation for those supplies that need to breathe. They should be easy to clean up with a damp cloth. The plastic is sturdy and feels as if it will hold up well. The framework is metal...lightweight but feels sturdy. All the parts slide together with minimal mechanical skills needed. There are screws where each piece joins together. Just line up the hole with a small slit and screw the enclosed screws in. This prevents the cart from accidentally coming apart during use. You do have to coax some of the pieces into place because they fit nice and tight. The most challenging part was the wheels. Two of them can be locked to prevent the cart from moving. They screw most of the way in very easily. After that, you tighten them the rest of the way with a wrench (all tools included!). A little awkward, but not difficult. Finished!This cart drives like a dream. Smooth and pretty quiet over our stone floors. The handle is a comfortable height for me. (I'm 5'3"-ish.).The real test was what the drag of the carpet would do, especially with supplies loaded on. It was easier than I have ever had with similar carts. Even with a full load of art supplies. I really love the handle on the long side of the cart. It makes it more manageable when rolling it along. With the swivel wheels, it is quite easy to drive. The base is built for stability and is wider than the shelves. In spite of that, I have a word of caution here. It is lightweight and moves so easily, I would not allow small children to use it as a toy. Safety first! I would also be cautious if you, or the person using it, has a balance issue. I have such issues and have not had problems, but for someone who loses balance and falls easily, it could move too easily and too quickly. I found it to move more easily than my walker. top_review: We loved these! I bought this for my 2 kiddos birthday party and we had everyone excited about it. Couldn't have been any easier start to finish and the colors were so bright! We had 8 people tye dying that day (4 adults 4 kids) and we still had a lot of product left. I gave the leftovers to my sister in law and she made a shirt with her niece. I will be ordering more of this. I had a couple similar looking dyes on here to choose and I went with this one. So glad I did.I have bought this kit 3 times now, and I love it! Colors stay bright after multiple washes (in cold or eco-warm-just because that's what I usually run the washer on). I made burp/spit up rags and crib sheets with the first batch so they have spent quite a bit of time in the washer, not to mention that I have soaked them in Oxyclean and it doesn't ruin the colors. The first 2 pictures are all the items I did with one single kit this last time (don't mind the gag gift boxers LOL). The final picture is from when I first tried this kit 15 months ago and it has survived well through all the washings and the Oxyclean soaks. I do suggest cotton fabric but I noticed that some brands put a thin waxy coating on their fabrics to keep it clean for shipping, so I just wash them on warm with just a little detergent and dry them before binding them. I had no problems with the brands Haines or Fruit of the Loom and didn't prewash them, but had to massage it a bit as I dyed them for full saturation. Here's what I did:1) I rubber band the fabrics I want to dye with the rubber bands included in the kit, but I also pick up an extra package or two of rubber bands just to make the designs more intricate.2) I fill each bottle with half the needed amount of water, replace the caps and shake well to dissolve all powder because sometimes the powder can get stuck to the bottom of the bottle. Then I fill the bottles up the rest of the way and shake again. WEAR GLOVES even at this stage or you will have to scrub for days to get it off your skin- like I did, which made my job interview the next day a bit awkward. Hah. ALSO, leave the bottles standing or tilted upright once filled as they tend to leak laying down.3) I lay out an old plastic shower curtain out in the yard in the shade, get comfortable with a drink and go to town- I use paper towels to wipe up spilled dye between switching colors so it doesn't transfer to other parts of my fabric. I work from lightest dye to darkest on each binded garmet. Also, if I noticed the dye was beading on the fabric and dripping off without absorbing, I just go slow and easy on the dye, and use a gloved finger to massage it in a bit so it will soak into the fabric then it would easily accept the dye when I add some more on.4) I put all the projects in a tightly knotted plastic garbage bag and leave them in the shaded garage overnight.5)The next day, I snip the rubber bands and use the garden hose to rinse out and wring out all of the garments. I suggest using running water from a hose or faucet instead of rinsing them in some sort of prefilled tub or basin to keep the white parts from soaking up leftover dye and being less vibrant.6) I hang them out to dry fully for a few hours, then I machine wash them on delicate, cold water with an extra rinse and spin. After first initial washing, I just toss them in with the rest of the laundry (except whites of course) and I have had no issues yet.Hope this helps!I’m so impressed with the amount of colors in this set. I used every color except for the black. My favorites were the purple, pink and turquoise together. We were able to dye shirts for the family and each person was thrilled with the gloves, rubber bands and dyes included. The colors held up well after washing. I’d recommend this set to anyone wanting a fun activity!Ordered this kit to do a craft with my grandkids ages 6 & 7. It came quickly and looked like the photo. Lots of colors to choose from and I liked that the kit included accessories such as plastic gloves and rubber bands. You should definitely use the gloves even when preparing the colors as some of the powder is likely on the outside of the bottles and will definitely stain. We used the kit outside and the directions were easy to follow and included tips for different patterns. My grands loved their tie-dyed shirts.Tulip has amazing dyes, and their kits are great for beginners. They include everything you'll need, and have a great range of colors.This was a hit at our day habilitation group when we did tie dye.Bright bold colorsWe tried this kit after using a more expensive brand (RIT) and a cheaper option (an off brand bought on Amazon). This kit was easy to prep and apply, comes with a great range of colors, and offers good value. Will definitely buy again for our next tie dye adventure.A brilliant gift for tweenage girls (and boys) ! My 11 year old had a tie dye party and her and her friends loved it :) all you need is included I provided 12 teeshirts and there was enough dye to decorate them all with some left over :)The dye works well and is easy to use, dont be fooled though, teh bottles are really small. I struggled to do a pair of sweatpants and a hoodie (adult sizes) in the same colours, i had to change my plan as the quantity just wasnt enoughIt’s a lot of dye - and therefore needs a lot of clothes. It also ran in the wash which means we all have tie dyed undies and socks and the colour has faded from what we intentionally dyed.Bought this as a gift, it went down pretty well and the person I gave it to later told me that it was the best kit that they had used so far, easy to use, less messy and such. I would say it's a successThis is the best quality , long lasting and vibrant dye I have ever used!! My daughter tie dyed a double duvets, three pillowcases and 2 t shirts with so much dye to spare!! The manual suggests good dye teqniques andI recommend putting one cup of white vinegar and salt in the wash with it as it makes the dye set more.

title: Valvoline Daily Protection 10W-30 Conventional Motor Oil 1 QT, Case of 6
description: What’s the best conventional motor oil for a daily driver? Consider Valvoline Daily Protection for your next oil change in a 2012 vehicle and older that doesn’t require a full synthetic. Available in SAE 10W-30, 10W-40, and 20W-50, Valvoline Daily Protection is engineered to safeguard motors from heat, wear, deposits and friction, the main reasons of engine breakdown. Formulated with premium-quality basestocks that protect engines against varnish deposits and contamination, the low-friction formulation helps optimize fuel economy, while quality anti-wear additives, combined with powerful detergents, fight sludge to help keep the engine clean. Valvoline Daily Protection meets the performance requirements of virtually all naturally aspirated and turbocharged and gasoline-fueled passenger cars and light duty trucks, like Dodge Ram, Toyota Tacoma, Toyota Camry, Honda Accord, Jeep Wrangler, Ford F150, Chevy Silverado and many more. Daily Protection provides high-temperature protection to resist breakdown in severe engine environments; low-temperature protection ensures the motor oil flows easily during cold winter weather, reducing wear at start-up. For outstanding performance day after day, count on Valvoline Daily Protection, made in America by the Original Motor Oil brand.

Wool dryer balls can be re-used for years, saving you hundreds of dollars. *Wool dryer balls are perfect for keeping your cloth diapers soft and chemical-free. *Wool dryer balls won't affect the absorbency of your towels, kitchen cloths, or cloth diapers - commercial softeners will. *100% wool dryer balls increase fluffiness and reduce static as dryer loads tumble. *Dryer balls help to soften clothes naturally. *Dryer balls are made from a renewable resource.How do they work? *It's simple. They bounce around in the dryer separating clothes, allowing more hot air to circulate through all the garments. As they tumble, the wool balls fluff your laundry, reduce wrinkles, and basically pummel the laundry to make it softer. *They do so much more than a dryer sheet by pulling moisture out of your clothes so you don't have to run the dryer as long. *The more dryer balls you have in a load, the shorter the drying time will be.Making felted wool dryer balls with yarn:Choosing Your Yarn: *Finding the right yarn is the most critical part of making these wool balls. top_review: I really enjoy the variety of colors that come in this pack of pens. I purchased the Fineliner Marker Pens by PIlot and was not impressed by the quality. I didn't like the pen that came with my Rocket Book Fusion. So these clicker pens are the in between option. I LOVE THEM! The only issue I have with them is that when I write in my RocketBook the pen "runs out of ink". I start writing and nothing comes out. I'm wondering if it's because there may still be water on the page from a previous use, or if the pen is truly running out of ink. I have also noticed that I have to wipe the pens with a tissue to get residual ink off the tip. Again, it hasn't stopped me from using it.Ok, so you are at a restaurant trying to seal a deal to have a new customer in your fast growing business. On the back of a napkin you make a proposal. You are about to hand the napkin over and you realize you added too many zeros. While the other person is distracted by the waitress asking if they needed anything else, you take it back and erase one "zero" off of the napkin. Not only can you do that with this pen, you will not tear the napkin or any other paper you write on. It is not a rubber eraser so there is no eraser pieces on the paper either. I like it.I love these, they're so much better than the old fashioned erasable pens that tore paper and didn't always erase. I do bookkeeping a couple days a week and often need to fix my mistakes. I also love them for ordinary writing.Pros: erases cleanly on most paper; ink writes smoothly; refillable; very comfortable.Cons: doesn't erase on cheap, rougher paper or on thermal paper like receipts; ink tends to run out quickly with heavy daily use; smudges occasionally.I typically need to change the ink cartridge every couple weeks or so. But they are well worth the cost if you tend to make a lot of mistakes when writing, like me. I love the feel of the pen and the ink flow. Several of my coworkers asked me about these, and I ended up ordering some for our office work.I have a middle school age nephew and he always asks me to buy him these pens. I figure if he is using them at school and likes them they just be goodThey write smooth and erase clean. I love the colors. My daughter actually stole this set from me so I bought another for myself. She uses them for note taking. I use mine for my planner.I bought these pens because you can mark fabrics with them, and once ironed the marks disappear. They are much more accurate to mark with than chalk and come in plenty of colors so they will show up nicely on different fabrics. Very happy with my purchase!Love these pens! Will always be a go to and was able to receive the same day. My local stores only sell black and colors are needed for visual purposed.I absolutely love Frixion pens and have used them for years! As a middle grades math teacher, they are so helpful! I have only used 2 of these pens and they have already run out of ink. I definitely want to keep the set, but am hopeful the company will send a replacement.I have the ADHD - I use these for notes and exams (and the corresponding highlighters) and It's made a world of difference for me. Being able to erase and re-write works so well. I also use it with a rocketbook (which was designed for them.)The colours are vibrant and the ink flows sooo nice. Erasing is a breeze. Profs and students always ask me about them.The *only* downside is, like many up ballpoints some colours go thin or dry out quickly, but, ballpoints.They've become my favourite pens. (get the clicker ones, not the ones with removable caps)I'm taking a copyediting / proofreading course and my instructor specifically recommended these PILOT pens. They're erasable ink! I've been using them for a few weeks now and also love them. These pens are not perfect - to start with, they are a bit pricey - but they are so unique they are worth the costs. The ink really does totally erase, using the built-in eraser tip. You'll never use all of the eraser top, so it's not a problem there.I do find that the ink can 'goop' a bit with these pens, but nothing terrible. And, after all, they are erasable. This particular tip is a fine point (0.7 mm) which I find easy to read. I've just ordered the super-fine tip (0.5 mm) set, so hopeful those will allow me a little more precision.I like how this is a multi-colour set, but I do wish there were more of the standard colours (more red, which is the most common copy-editing colour to use). In any event, these would be great pens to also give kids, as you can erase their work if needed - although I haven't tried other surfaces than paper lol.In sum, these are great, unique gel ink pens, and definitely worth the money!Pros: It erases and is much handier than using white-out. They are colourful pens.Cons: If you write on both sides of thin paper (think loose leaf), you will likely erase some writing on the back side of the page when you erase on the other side. If you write with firm pressure, the ink does not flow out evenly and you get light streaks and the writing experience doesn't feel very smooth. With lighter pressure, it's perfectly fine. The pen feels cheap and the clicker makes a light noise as you write which adds to the cheap feel.I like these pens for specific purposes, but if you don't make mistakes very often and are looking for a smooth pen, I would choose something else.I really wanted to love these pens! I have written to Pilot regarding warranty but have not heard back. Some good customer service would give me restored hope in this product. We'll see....The pens are comfortable, erasable, and work great with the Rocketbook. However these pens have barely lasted a week and a 3 pages of writing! 2 pens in one pack ran out in that time span and the other ones look on track to do the same. I've seen some comments saying that recent purchases are not lasting long so maybe they changed their formula or had a bad batch. Currently, these are NOT worth the price.

top_review: Ernie Ball has a solid reputation for quality in the guitar world, and their flat ribbon patch cables generally live up to that standard. This 24-inch black version (P06228) is a decent option for connecting your pedals on a tight board.Here's a breakdown of the pros and cons:Pros:Space Saving: The flat ribbon design is the key selling point. It allows for much tighter pedal spacing compared to traditional bulky cables, maximizing real estate on your pedalboard. This is especially crucial for smaller boards.Clean Look: The black color and slim profile contribute to a cleaner, more organized pedalboard aesthetic.Decent Signal Quality: While not the absolute best in terms of signal integrity compared to super high-end cables, the Ernie Ball patch cables generally provide a clear signal with minimal tone loss, especially over shorter distances like this 24-inch version.Durable Construction (Generally): Ernie Ball typically uses quality materials, and these cables feel relatively robust. The molded connectors seem well-attached. (However, see the cons below).Reasonably Priced: These cables are often available at a competitive price point, making them a good value for the space-saving benefits they offer.Cons:Durability Concerns (Potentially): While the materials seem decent, some users have reported issues with the connectors eventually wearing out or becoming loose over time, especially with frequent bending and manipulation. This is a common complaint with flat ribbon cables in general, as the thin design can be more susceptible to stress.Signal Degradation (Possible): While decent, the signal isn't flawless. Demanding players with highly sensitive ears might notice a slight loss of high frequencies compared to more premium cables.Stiffness: Due to the flat ribbon design, these cables can be somewhat stiff, which can make routing them in complex configurations a bit challenging.Overall:The Ernie Ball Flat Ribbon Patch Cable (24in, Black - P06228) is a solid choice for guitarists looking to maximize space on their pedalboards. The flat design is a major advantage, and the signal quality is generally good enough for most players. However, be aware of the potential durability concerns and the slight stiffness of the cable. For the price, it's a good option, but if you're seeking absolute top-tier signal clarity and rock-solid durability, you might want to explore more premium (and often more expensive) alternatives.Final Verdict: Good for maximizing space and a clean look, but be mindful of potential durability issues.

description: The Crop-A-Dile 2 Big Bite Punch by We R Memory Keepers is an all-in-one tool for punching, setting, and embellishing every crafting project. top_review: Had a standard Crop-a-Dile. It was good but the WR CADII Big Bite Blue is so much better.First it stands on its own, so you don’t have to struggle with holding/balancing it. Other plier-style punches work fine for narrow items like belts, etc., but if you need to punch holes in a spot further from the edge of the material, like in a hat or jeans, you need a longer reach (or to use a traditional hammer-and-anvil punch). Fold an 8.5 x 11 sheet of paper 4 times, or cut a thin sheet of cardboard into quarters.2. Place the cardboard or folded paper behind the fabric, as a stiffer backing.3. Punch a hole through both the fabric and the backing to cut a clean-edged hole.4. I looked at so many stores in my area and the prices on Amazon are SO much better. It took only 2 days to deliver right to my front door. I couldn't be happier!! :)Beautiful vivid colors in a nice selection of tones and hues. Smooth even lay down, wibt skip or hop on the page. I'd always had difficulty wirh colored pencils (too hard, breakage, poor saturation, etc) until I tried a set of 12 I received as a gift. I have several sets and love them all. Great for kids, adults, beginners or experienced artists.This is a very good product. And came very neat.Works very well😀They are the bestPrismacolor is amazing.Amazing Colored Pencils! Super smooth , like butter. I recommend these for any artist , great pigment! Overall best colored pencils i've ever used.I've been doing pen and ink artwork (and some airbrush) since 1976. I didn't stray far from that, but over the years, I'd say a half a dozen times I've purchased a small set of color pencils to test out doing color.Disappointed every time. I didn't want to buy expensive ones so it's so obvious now what the problem was. Also, I tried water color pencils and I just don't care for the look, but the others were all cheapo sets.i picked up the urge again to try color recently. I've been doing a lot of chip carving lately, and it got me back into that 'artist' side. I have been doing motion graphics, and graphic design for about 15 years, so I'd gotten away from the real artwork, done by hand.I started reading reviews and it was obvious very quickly that Prismacolor was going to be the right one. I opted for the premier as all the tutorials and reviews I read/watched showed them.I finally decided to get this set. the Premier 48 w/tin. Let's just say that within 10 minutes I knew that my whole work of artwork had just changed. It was instantly obvious this is what i needed.now, let's all admit, there were some advancements in color pencils a few years back that really changed things. i'd kind of thought about it since then, but never got the urge until recentlyif you are like me and had never tried a professional quality set, but are looking now, you will be shocked at how well these work. The way they blend and build is hard to describe. I am absolutely in love with them.The big pros for me, are;1. Tthey have very soft cores so they are very smooth to work with.2. Even though the cores are soft, they are also thick. They do not break. At least in the time I've had them they haven't. not a single break yet, and frankly that was one of my disappointments of every other set i tried. (tip, get a decent sharpener, i like the Prismacolor sharpener here http://www.amazon.com/dp/B004ZDL0K2/ref=wl_it_dp_o_pC_nS_ttl?_encoding=UTF8&colid=2MUG68SOZ3Z4A&coliid=I27HS01U8F39HZ but the tip is, hold the pencil stationary and rotate the sharpener, not the pencil. works great!) A decent sharpener makes a very big difference3. The amount of complimentary shades that come with even the 48 pack is nice. I do wish I'd gotten the 72 now, but i wasn't sure about using them at all. I will be replacing these with the 72 next time.cons;none, if I had to find one, it would be price and really it's not that bad anyway.. I know we all like to save money, but this low of a cost for something that provides so much is just flat out a bargain. I considered trying copic markers a while back. get a few hundred out if you want to try that. This is cheap.Once you switch to Prismacolor, you won't want anything else. This is what my daughter and her art teacher both have said. And her teacher was right. But these are amazing quality pencils. The tin case is good quality as well to keep your investment organized.Recently took up drawing again and it seems these were the pencils to have. Really happy with these and the quality is incredible, I've put a photo of the same drawing done with standard pencils and then with the prismacolor. The difference is amazing and it does seem to bring a bit more life to the image. (Probably the more talented folk could do this a lot better but hey) the pencils have a waxy feel when used and real easy to blend, they also come in a nifty little tin.Expensive but worth every penny. I bought the £24 tin and there are plenty of colours. There's also a smaller tin that's around £12 if that's a little pricey.Ich habe bereits zur größeren Palette eine ausführliche Rezension geschrieben, habe aber über die Jahre viele verschiedene Paletten verbraucht und besitze einige, darunter auch 2 Prismacolor Paletten (einmal 48 einmal 132 Farben). Nach all der Zeit kann ich manchen Rezensionen immer noch nicht zustimmen, es sind natürlich nicht die allerbesten Stifte auf dem Markt, aber sie sind auch bei weitem (!) nicht so schlecht wie sie dargestellt werden. Wer sich für Prismacolor entscheidet sollte ungefähr wissen, worauf er / sie sich einlässt, daher schreibe ich die Fakten kurz zusammen:Positiv:- Farbauswahl bis zu 150 Stiften- sehr weicher Farbauftrag mit sehr satten und leuchtenden Farben, ich vergleiche die Prismacolor mit teureren Stiften a la Polychromo, Luminance und Coloursoft- weiche Minen und stilistische Stifte ohne zusätzlichen Verziehrungen- die Farben decken super auf schwarzem oder grauem (Tonpapier, Fotokarton etc.) Zeichenpapier, auf getöntem Papier leuchten sie richtig- sehr einfach zu mischen, lassen sich sehr gut vermischen- guter PreisNegativ:- fast keine Einzelstifte zu kaufen, das heißt sobald ein Stift aufgebraucht ist, müsst ihr die ganze Palette wohl neu kaufen.- Layern / Schichten nur sehr begrenzt möglich, nach 2 bis maximal 3 Schichten bildet sich ein deutlicher Wax Bloom (weiße Schichte über der eigentlichen Farbe, das Papier nimmt danach keine Farbpartikel mehr auf)Vorurteil:- angeblich brechen Prismacolor extrem oft, dem kann ich allerdings nach vielen Jahren, nicht zustimmen. Meine Stifte ließen sich immer gut anspitzen, ich hatte auch noch nie einen Sanford Stift, der ständig abgebrochen ist. Wobei ich den Faber Castell Multispitzer verwende und noch nie ein Problem hatte.- angeblich sind die Minen nicht zentriert, auch das habe ich bisher selten gesehen, wobei ich sagen muss, dass man es nicht so stark merkt wenn eine Mine bei einem Stift 1mm schief im Schaft sitzt. Vielleicht zeichne ich dafür auch schon zu lange und bemerke es nicht mehr?Hier auf jedenfalls zwei Bilder die mit Prismacolor von Sanford gestaltet wurden, denn im Grunde sprechen Bilder mehr als Worte und wir suchen daher nach idealen Farbstiften.My first time trying these, and I have to say they are worth the hype! I have a set of 120 Faber Castell Polychromos, which is lovely but impractical to carry around, so I needed something smaller for various outings and travel. The Prismacolor pencils were a cheaper but equally reputable option. I only got the set today; but after sketching for a bit I found they are smooth and easy to use, and the colors are rich and blend well together. The metal box they come in is also well-designed, so I was able to place it vertically in my backpack without it opening (this is surprisingly rare). description: Product Description When minor injuries occur it's important to clean and treat wounds properly to reduce the risk of infection, Savlon Cream will help you with that. Savlon Antiseptic Cream is suitable for both adults and children to cleanse and reduce the risk of infection in minor wounds, cuts and grazes, and superficial burns. How to use: Clean and dry the affected area thoroughly, gently apply the cream using clean hands. Apply a small amount to the affected area and repeat the application as required. For external use only. Avoid contact with the eyes, middle ear, meninges and other nervous tissues. If you experience any side effects or allergic reactions stop using immediately and seek medical advice. Always read the label. Suitable for all members of your family. Store all medicines out of sight and reach of children and pets. Do not store above 25 degrees Celcius. Do not use after the expiry date shown on the end of the tube. Use within 12 months of opening. If symptoms persist, please consult your GP. Do not use if you are allergic to any of the ingredients, especially Chlorhexidine as it may cause allergic reactions. Cetostearyl alcohol may cause local skin reactions. Parahydroxybenzoates may cause allergic reactions (possibly delayed). While allergic reactions are rare stop using and seek medical help if you experience: difficulty breathing, swelling of the face, tongue or throat, dizziness, skin irritation or rash. Savlon Antiseptic Cream contains the active substances Cetrimide and Chlorhexidine Digluconate. It is used for the cleansing and prevention of skin infections in first aid (minor burns, small wounds, insect bites and stings) and minor skin problems (including blisters and sores, chapped skin, nappy rash, spots, blackheads and sunburn). Always use this medicine exactly as described in this leaflet or as your doctor or pharmacist have told you. Check with your doctor or pharmacist if you are not sure. Wash hands thoroughly before and after the application. Clean the affected area with clean water and pat dry. Gently apply the cream to the wound using your fingers or gauze. For cuts and small wounds, protect the affected area with a plaster or non-adherent dressing. Burns and scalds are left uncovered. top_review: These are a game changer for sleeping in late. I have blinds in my bedroom window. While they provide privacy, they do not block the light out well. I had purchased some other blackout curtains locally, but they had a sprayed on backing and I could only find the 63 inch with grommets. I learned grommets let the light in. These curtains actually have a nice black lining. They are not made out of that stiff material a lot of black out curtains are made out of. These hang nicely. If you want your room to be truly dark, I would recommend hanging these on a curtain rod that curves to the wall so the curtain can be pulled to the edge. I orginally had the decorative rod and it left too much of a gap between the wall and the curtain. I got the 63 inch curtains and light does shine in through the bottom. I am sure the longer pair would have darkened my room much better. Unfortunately, longer curtains are a cat hair magnet.  I did wash and dry these prior to hanging them. I also steamed them to get some of the wrinkles out. I think the weight of the longer curtains would also help them to drape better. I can now sleep in later and darkening the room for naps is great. I will add pictures soon.Update: I added pictures. It is difficult to get a good picture to show the darkened room. My camera either makes it too dark or too light. It looks like the picture I attached got even darker when I shared it. The room gets dark enough that I can sleep, but there is still enough light that I can walk around the room without stumbling into anything. I attached pictures of the curved hanging rod which I did purchase on Amazon. I have a double rod because I have sheer panels underneath the dark out curtains.

top_review: While moving into our home a few years ago, somehow our box grater and one-handled cheese graters were lost. Since then I’ve been dragging out the trusty old’ Cuisinart food processor when I’ve needed to shred cheese… which is a quite literally a pain (I have severe DDD) and creates a lot of unnecessary clean up. Because my Microplane grater (which thankfully didn’t become lost in the move) does such a great job zesting citrus and grating fine things, I decided to stick with Microplane, and I’m glad I did!This little grater is amazing! It’s much more handy and takes up a lot less room than an old fashioned, bulky box grater. With a box grater, you need to have a stable surface so you can grate over a plate or paper towel, but you still have to keep it stable with one hand. With this, you can lay the grater horizontally over the top of a plate, bowl, pot or pan, or just hold it at an angle over a dish while you grate, and you don’t need to take up any additional counter space do it! If I wanted to grate huge quantities of food, like multiple heads of cabbage for making sauerkraut or kimchi, I might still break out the food processor, but for 99% of what I need, this handheld grater is so much easier to use! I’d much rather grate a 2 lb block of cheese with this than break out the food processor, swap out the blade for a shredding disc, then deal with clean up of the food processor bowl, cover, food pusher and grating disc (that also would take up a lot of real estate inside the dishwasher).This thing is razor SHARP, so it makes grating much easier than an old fashioned type grater because you don’t have to use as much force. I don’t have the strength I used to have, so I’m thankful for this. You might want to use a cut proof glove for grating, or at least pay very close attention, especially if you’re accustomed using an older style grater. I’ve shredded sharp cheddar cheeses, softer Muenster and Colby cheeses, and it does an excellent job at creating long shreds. Softer cheeses can benefit from a few minutes in the freezer before shredding, but I’ve never had any issues.Clean up with a dish sponge or brush is easy, as long as you clean up soon after using. Just make sure to clean and dry “with the grain” of the shredding holes, and not against, or you’ll shred your sponge or dish towel. I don’t put mine into the dishwasher because I don’t place my expensive knives in there, either. It might be fine to do this once in a while, but I still don’t, since the high heat and detergent chemicals are not exactly the best for sharp blades. This is much easier to clean than the box graters I’ve had, because it was always a pain to reach up I inside to get them thoroughly clean. Love this! I’ll probably purchase additional Microplane graters at some point, to have a variety of shred sizes to choose from. Professional chefs use this style and brand for VERY good reason!

top_review: The first thing to say about people not liking the flavor of this olive oil is that if you don't want robust, don't buy robust. Of course it's more "bitter" than a light oil (which with olives just means full flavored - try eating a raw, uncured olive sometime). There are different types of oil derived from different olive types, ages, ripeness, condition, and pressing for a reason. Grungy, earthy, robust happens to be one of my favorites for many things outside of deep frying. If it's not yours, you should definitely buy the high priced light stuff and not complain that low brow should be the same as high brow. The flavor of this oil is exactly what it should be: rich, raw, tangy, and earthy.As to not turning cloudy or thick in the refrigerator, it does. Maybe some people are just expecting too much reaction or at too high a temperature, but all oils congeal at low temperatures, so that is not an indication it's mixed with other oils. All vegetable oils congeal at about the same temperature. What makes it not congeal until much lower temperatures is the amount of filtering, which can remove some of the polyphenols and wax. Basically people are complaining that this oil is cleaned. While unfiltered might be a cool buzzword in olive oil trends, you do not want unfiltered with the olives they use for "robust."Finally, yes the olives for this particular bottle are grown in different countries. Pompeian has farms all over the world. If you want single source from Spain, get Pompeian's Bold EVOO, which is clearly marked as being exclusively Spanish. There is no subterfuge here. Pompeian is very cooperative about disclosures and they have about every kind of olive oil you could want. You just have to know what you're buying. You wouldn't buy a table wine and complain it wasn't all Sangiovese. You can't buy Robust clearly marked as having olives from all over and complain it's not single source. Pretty common sense. If you want to be an olive oil expert, you'll have to start looking at it more like wine than vegetable oil, because the selection process is largely the same on basics.So, what makes me such a smart guy you should listen to? Well first I'm a chef, and a fairly accomplished one. Second, my family is Italian and we grow olives. I just wanted to take a minute not only to give Pompeian their due props, but to set the record straight for anybody confused by the misinformation in the few negative outbursts. This is exactly what it says it is, and it's fantastic. It just has to be what you want.

top_review: Despite the baffling instruction sheet, it really is as easy to install as the video suggests. I had wood strip runners made thinking I needed to clear the lip in my cupboard. However the brace elements attached beneath the unit, sort of like very flat "u" shaped legs spanning the width of the unit, were high enough that the mechanism tidily cleared the lip. In short: truly was 1-2-3-4 screws and zip, drawer in place. Smooth action even fully loaded is a dream. Dimensions reliable, at least on the units I bought late 2024. Drawers fully extend. I especially liked the oval-shaped screw holes, which allow you to refine positioning before tightening the screws all the way down. I will buy more.One thing worth mentioning: normally one wouldn't install a unit like this on an upper shelf if the shelf is adjustable. However I just drilled a hole just above the shelf in position and tapped in another shelf-holder nib in place *above* the back of each side of the adjustable shelf to secure it from tipping with a weighted drawer installed. Worked like a charm. Transformed my extremely limited cabinet space and saves my knees. I did have to remove the top shelf and install the base of the second unit before putting the shelf back into place. This was only because there wasn't enough room to get head and shoulders in there above the moveable shelf to screw in the base of the drawer unit. Just placed the shelf back where I wanted and then snapped the drawer into its extension rail mechanism. Brilliant design, strong materials and sturdy action.

title: Fiskars PowerArc Utility Snips (8 Inch)
description: Experience advanced mechanics and ergonomics with a new generation of cutting tools that deliver more strength, comfort and control. PowerArc Utility Snips boast intelligently curved blades that alter the angle between blades to give you over 2X more power, especially during the toughest part of the cut. An offset design with heavy-duty stainless steel blades can be used to cut materials from above or below, keeping waste material away from your hand. In addition, an ergonomic, spring-assisted handle helps reduce hand fatigue and features Softgrip for enhanced dexterity and comfort. A serrated edge, extended tang and bolted joint improve control and durability.
categories: ["Tools & Home Improvement","Power & Hand Tools","Hand Tools","Nippers & Snips"]
top_review: The particular Fiskars model shears with the open-top-handle is really GREAT!  I compared it against one of Fiskars' other models (selling out of the same Amazon listing) with fully closed loops for both the top and bottom of the handle, and this one is quite superior, providing more leverage while cutting, therefore it's easier on your hand and muscles, AND more effective at cutting. Plus, the blades are SHARP, and strong.The other Fiskars model wasn't bad at all, it was quite good, it's just that this one is significantly better; and its greater ease of cutting is quite noticeable and comes in handy when cutting cardboard boxes, as I do (from Amazon deliveries!). This design with the open top handle and the wide-loop bottom handle (the latter allows more fingers to hold it) not only provides more cutting leverage, but allows you to get whatever material you're cutting out of your way as you cut further and further into it.I also compared this item with yet another set of shears, that one purchased at Home Depot (made by Wiss), but it was definitely a nice set of shears that did a good job. It's just that this Fiskars model clearly does a better job-- it cuts better, cuts thicker materials, and is much easier to cut with, with more leverage, therefore easier on your hand.I don't know how long these Fiskars will last, what with the open, uncovered spring that I wonder if it might become detached, but I bought three of these-- two more after being so pleased with the first one-- and they all three work equally great.By the way, there is a little plastic piece at the bottom of the handle that locks the two-piece handle together so that the blades stay together when stored. (I can see where that lock could easily become undone, however, but so far, that hasn't happened to me.)This is really a phenomenal product, and I can not only cut through thick cardboard boxes with it (I much prefer using this to a box cutter), I can also cut through double-thickness of those boxes when necessary; though there is a bit more difficulty then.I highly recommend this product for its intended uses. And don't let the unusual look of the handle scare you away-- it's actually one of the great features on this set of shears.(By the way, I was drawn to look at Fiskars shears in the first place by reading some other reviewer's recommendation for them!!-- although, of all places, it was in an Amazon review of a set of screwdrivers, where the reviewer was commenting how difficult it was to open that package of screwdrivers with all of the clear plastic glued to cardboard, but that these Fiskars shears made it a lot easier! Reading that screwdriver set review resulted in my buying three pairs of these Fiskars shears!)

As a fan of BTS and LEGO, this set uniquely blends my passions, offering an immersive building experience that captures the vibrant essence of the band's iconic "Dynamite" music video. Each figure is beautifully crafted, showcasing the distinct personalities and styles of the band members, making them an awesome and unique addition to any collection. The inclusion of detailed instructions and the LEGO Builder app enhances the building experience, making it accessible to builders of all skill levels. The LEGO® Ideas BTS Dynamite set is more than just a LEGO set; it's a tribute to the global phenomenon that is BTS, offering a unique way for fans to celebrate their love for the band. It's a must-have for BTS ARMY and LEGO enthusiasts alike.

top_review: I could have purchased an after-market brand for my P-touch PT-1800 label machine for less money, but I did not know for certain it would be compatible with my machine, or have the same adhesion properties as the OEM tape.The Fluorescent Orange is a good offset color match for Milwaukee Packout and tools. You will need more than one once you start labeling. It is not a perfect match, but the colors offset themselves very nicely.Pretty straightforward, this is the real deal. Drops into my machine easily and quality of print and adhesion is great. I label everything from install dates on electrical items to my kids' water bottles and thermos. They withstand water pretty well as I don't have to replace it every wash. Now that I think about it, it's been months since I have noticed and peeling at all.I may or may not have labeled the dogs, the wife and the me with it. She wasn’t amused (maybe a little). Also, pretty wild that the adhesive holds up in the dishwasher, yet comes off clean and relatively easy when you want it to.product arrived damagedSecond purchase great quality original Brand work very well for labeling & tagging storage items. Very visible & easy to read & durable. Cheaper options available but these have worked very well and the quality is great.What tamper evident means is that, while it's possible to peel this tape off, doing so messes up the tape such that there is no way to re-stick it so that your screwing about isn't obvious. Let's say you want to place serial numbers on your capital equipment. It would become impossible for someone to move your serial number from one computer (for example) to another. Also, when the tape is peeled off, half the adhesive remains on the tape while half is left on the object--and depending on the age of the tape it can be anywhere from darn difficult (fresh) to darn damn hellishly difficult (several years old) to clean the adhesive off the object.The white background color is the adhesive. When peeled up it leaves a checkerboard pattern of stuck-to-tape/stuck-to-object (3mm squares). So you get small white squares of goo left on the object. If not careful while handling the tape before you stick it down, bits of adhesive can stick to your fingers. This leaves clear "holes" along the edges of your label. Also, Brother changed the construction of the tape a few years ago. The newer tape is thinner and more flexible--a plus IMO. Brother's tamper evident tape comes only in this color and only in this width.Anyway, it's not that some dirty-rat-bastard won't ever be able to remove your labels, but that they will never be able to reuse your labels somewhere else. If this is what you want then this is the label tape for you.The red color in the text was bright and vibrant. It was perfect for making new labels in a large size.After using the original Brother tapes I thought them too expensive so I bought alternative tapes - much cheaper. What a load of rubbish - every single tape seized after a short time. OK - so the originals are more expensive but I have never had any issues. I use them for labelling plants and shrubs outdoors - excellent.Bit of a con, I Returned the item.Not a lot to say really but its a lot neater and smarter than white tape with black print when levelling items such as camera bodies and lenses.These TZ tapes are a lot thinner than the earlier Brother tape systems which is a big plus when trying to stick them to curved surfaces.Handsome gold-on-black adhesive tape, with multiple uses around the home. It's non-fading and weatherproof, so can also be used in the garden. I use it for labelling plugs and frozen meals. However, I don't understand why a product, which is basically a roll of tape, has to cost so much.If you have an OCD about labelling everything you own and your handwriting is rubbish, buy a labeller, and if you like the fact that you can have black text on yellow labels, you should probably buy this!

top_review: Seafarers is a great addition to Catan. It adds 9 new game play options, each with a slightly different board setup and rules. The 9th scenario allows you to build your own world, while following a few simple instructions or create it all on your own. While 2 people can play, it's much more fun with 3 or more.From what I researched before buying the Seafarers expansion, this is easier to learn than some other expansion sets and a big favorite of Catan lovers.As always, the instructions are pretty clear and have images and examples, but watching a couple of YouTube videos showing set up and game play can make it much easier to get started.Don't forget that this is an expansion set and you need the original Catan board game in addition to Seafarers. This is for up to 4 players, there are extension sets for 5-6 players that you can get separately.Catan is a family favorite, whenever we get together. Playing Seafarers has added so many fun options.A good value, arrived quickly and in great condition. I'm very happy with this purchase.We've played Settlers for years but have only recently started trying the expansions. We have had a lot of fun with this one, bringing some new and different strategies to the game without making it overcomplicated.Although I’ve only played through the first scenario with my board game group, I can already tell this is going to be a pleasant expansion. It feels so exciting and new! I love the concept of exploring unknown islands and I love the later concepts of pirate lairs, fish gathering, and spice smuggling that I haven’t gotten to you. Overall this expansion offers a world of new content. It may seem overwhelming at first, but each scenario builds off the previous, making it easy to learn in bite sized chunks. I plan on buying more expansions in the future!Traders and Barbarians adds several scenarios to play.Its great to mix them with other expansions. It worth it if you play often and don't mind if the games take a little longer.me ha servido para integrar a todos los miembros de la familia desde los más pequeños hasta los abuelos.Great collection of new variants for Settlers of Catan - we especially like the 2-player rules (we tried to make some on our own, but these are well-constructed), the Fishermen of Catan, and using the cards vs. rolling dice.Garantiza horas de diversión. Solo toma un poco de tiempo entender completamente como jugarlo, ya que si lleva un nivel de complejidad algo elevado.This is a must add on for allowing additional players.Chosen as an add on to the original Catan which we bought at christmas, and loved. This was the expansion that seemed most popular (through a quick Google and reading reviews on board game sites that compared the various expansions available). Quick note - the ones labelled 'expansion' expand the game, as in create new goals and ways of earning victory points as well as physically expanding the size of the board, while 'extension' packs give you extra pieces so you can have more players - be careful which you end up buying because it isn't always clear from cut and pasted product descriptions!Our family (two adults, two teens aged 13 and 14) loved the original game but after enough games it can get a bit tedious, and so opted for this expansion. We're adding a single extra element at a time (there are several 'senarios' in this - you add extra islands, then pirates, then fish, then spices, but you can play with only one extra (pirates/fish/spices) at a time, or add each to the previous so first you play with extra islands, then extra islands and pirates, then extra islands and pirates and fish and so on. What we decided to do was add each new element and get comfortable playing that (so maybe four or five games) before then adding the next thing in, and that's working well for us - our thinking is that once we've played a game without having to check back in the booklet to clarify any rules or had any disputes along the lines of "But you already moved your ship so now it's too late to trade gold to get sheep to buy more moves for the ship" vs "No, because it has sheep for moves under the movement phase" countered with "but you're not using a sheep, you're trading gold for it THEN using it" then we have got our heads round it enough to add in something else.Add a lot of interest to the basic game, with much more going on and more things to keep track of, as well as being played on a physically larger board so do think about whether it will fit where you play! I'd highly recommended this expansion (though haven't personally played any of the other expansions so can't compare with them), but do keep in mind you need to use lots of pieces from the basic game so don't get this unless you already have ordinary basic Catan, as it will be useless!All in all, adds extra layers to the game, making it much more strategic and enjoyable.Um, it's Catan. I purchased it to divide my friends and family and cause massive rifts that ended up in bloodshed and tears. My ten-year-old son decided blocking my biggest resources was a good idea and now? Well... He lives in the yard. Great game, super fun, will be buying all of them!**Catan House Rules state any and all fighting, name calling, backstabbing, scheming, threats, and contracts made while within playing time of the game become null and void once the game has ended, and may never be referenced or spoken of again until the start of a new game.A great addition to the base game, and while it seems like a small addition and is the lightest expansion in comparison, it does change the game up and makes it more dynamic as well as offering 8 different scenarios to set your board up and 1 where it's completely up to you instead of the small island you're stuck on in the base game, which freshens up the game a lot if you were bored by the recurring theme of regular Catan.It's not only a good setting stone to other expansions, as this is the easiest to grasp, if you desire it's also the best expansion to combine with another, most commonly with Cities & Knights, which in terms of added gameplay it adds the most depth and strategy (and with it complexity making it a bit too much for a family game, so know what you're getting into).All in all, a fresh of breath air if you've grown stale of regular Catan and want more, but not that much more you're overwhelmed, this little thing adds a lot to your games of Catan.We bought this to go with our 'Settlers of Catan' game so that more people could play. We were very confused as none of the pieces would match up and then we realised that the game has a new producer and has changed all the pieces. So if you want to buy this extension pack you have to have the 'CATAN' game not 'Settlers of Catan'. We did email the new producers but they did not respond at all. So you need to buy two new games. Disappointing.I bought this as a gift and was hugely disappointed and upset that I received a fake set. Not only did the set contain fake pieces, but also did not work properly with the original set and so completely defeats the purpose of an expansion pack.Photo #1 - The small brown house on the right is a settlement (which is fine) and the small/ flat brown roof on the left is supposedly a settlement... but is clearly a very faulty/ fake piece.Photo #2 - Note how the additional pieces that expand the original 4 player board do not fit properlyPhoto #3 - Due to the poor fitting when removing the additional pieces they actually damage the original set and start splitting the card in half

top_review: A couple months ago I redecorated a bedroom for my grandson who moved in to go to college.  I must have looked at every curtain on Amazon before deciding.  One thing I wish was different is that the backing be white, not black.  The upstairs bedroom is in the back of the house, so it's ok anyway, but white backing is usually preferred.Good value for the money, the drapes have a good thickness to them, and perfect at blocking out light and cold and heat.  The grommets make them easy to install and various lengths are available for any ceiling height.  They look great in his room.  I'm posting a couple pictures to show how I brought the room together around these curtains.  One photo is a design board I put together as I was gathering all the items needed to create a whole new bedroom for my grandson.

Buscaba algo así ya que como muchos adaptadores son de gran tamaño ocupan dos espacios en regletas tradicionales y una llega a no ser suficiente, pero con esta puedo conectar todo, es muy conveniente para mí. También, como vivo en una ciudad donde regularmente hay apagones de luz, me era vital encontrar un aparato que tuviera protección contra altas tensiones.Eso sí, me gustaría que tuviera un sistema para que cada lado de la regleta fuera independiente y poder apagar cada lado con un botón, ya que el botón que trae abarca toda la regleta; si lo apagas, apagas toda la regleta, pero de ahí en fuera, estoy muy satisfecha con mi compra.Me encanto lo tengo para organizar mi escritorio y poder conectar varias cosas, es demasiado largo que casi no lo utilizo completamente, los materiales son de buena calidad, nunca he tenido ningún problema con el voltaje. title: Zerex Asian Vehicle Blue Silicate and Borate Free 50/50 Prediluted Ready-to-Use Antifreeze/Coolant 1 GA
description: Zerex from Valvoline is the #1 selling OEM-approved coolant brand. Zerex Asian Vehicle Blue Antifreeze/Coolant is proven to maximize engine life in vehicles made by Asian auto manufacturers such as Acura, Honda, Infiniti, Nissan and others which specify a blue formula that’s silicate and borate-free with HOAT (Hybrid Organic Acid Technology). Specially formulated with a phosphate additive, Zerex is made for your car and protects better than industry standards against corrosion, leaking, deposits as well as freezing and boiling – the four main causes of cooling system failure, which is the leading cause of engine breakdown. Our HOAT formula includes a special phosphate additive that protects from corrosion, scale and rust, so radiators, water pumps and other metal cooling system parts (including aluminum) stay clean and your antifreeze flows and functions properly. Zerex Asian Vehicle Blue Antifreeze/Coolant contains no silicates, borates, 2-EHA, amines or nitrites. So whether you’re topping off your radiator or doing a complete system flush, trust Zerex Asian Vehicle Blue Antifreeze/Coolant. Made for your car. Made by Valvoline.

top_review: In motorcycles, you can use propylene glycol, it's less toxic. Or you can use Xerex Asian Blue.This is almost the same as the Suzuki Blue which is used in new Suzuki motorcycles. I put this in a 2008 Suzuki motorcycle.The Asian Green/Asian Blue/Asian Red Xerex products are the same. So pick a color.Asian blue has no silicates, which can ruin the high speed water pump on a motorcycle. Asian blue also has no 2-EHA. Recall that 2-EHA completely destroys your engine, and it should be outlawed. PEAK decided to add 2-EHA to their standard "universal" green antifreeze, because they want to destroy everyone's car (in my opinion). They charge extra money now to get the non 2-EHA product.I would advise using the XEREX Asian antifreeze for your car or motorcycle, or tractor. It's the best product there is right now on the market, unless you switch to a less effective non-toxic propylene glycol product (if you want less toxicity).

top_review: If you don't want to mess with a technical illustration pen, these are the next best thing. Solid black, (or colors) draw crisp lines with no bleed. great for the experienced artist or the novelist doodler!Great Deal. Good Product.C'mon. You know these pens. Buying from AMZ, you just hope they've not dried out sitting in a warehouse for ages. I'm not artistic - just messy writer and these help me write more legibly in different colors and different colors without smearing. I love them. They are $$$.These are a great set of pens that are very pigmented and write very thin without feeling scratchy on the paper. I know these are more artists pens but I use them more for writing in my textbooks in a color coordinated way. I got these specifically too because dry very fast, even on very glossy paper so these is little to no smearing because it dries so fast (not immediately but much much faster than say a gel pen). Maybe a little overkill and pricy for my usage but these pens fit exactly the niche I was looking for but I can't speak for the aspects that artists are looking for. They are some of the thinnest color pens set available (I think the brand makes a pen set that's slightly thinner with the same colors) so you can write a lot in even small margins but it is still very clear and readable. Also, the pens seem very high quality and durable. Even the fine tip hasn't bent on me yet even though I write with it a lot and don't always take care of them as well as I should and the ink hasn't dried on me even after lots of use and forgetting to put a cap on one of them for a few hours. The pen still worked fine and the ink was still very pigmentedThe cons I would say are that despite the high quality, the writing and text around the pen fades very quickly and is rubbed/scratched off from even just mild friction in a pencil case. This is more of a minor gripe because it makes the pens look older than they really are. I guess it gives the pens character but very minor nitpick. The thing that I don't like is that the set is missing an orange color. The pens colors are black, brown, pink, the primary colors except for yellow, and the secondary colors except for orange. Instead of yellow or orange, it's replaced with this sepia/dark orange/light brown color. I get that yellow is probably too light to make a pen for, but I was hoping for a nice bright orange color to complete the set. I think drawers and artists will probably like the sepia color more but I would have prefered a bright orange instead because it looks much nicer when color coordinating and it would round out the color story I think. That's just a personal preference and rant.Other than that, they are slightly expensive pens but they are quality and very much worth it. I would recommend them.I like that the end tip is colored so that I can store them tip down, thus reducing the chance of the tips drying out. There is a clip in the side of the cap which allows you to carry them in the pocket without them falling out. Also the end cap has the color of the pen as well as the tip size; this is so handy to easily identify which pen your looking for if you store different colors and tip sizes together. They are a nice size; not bulky or awkward in the hand. I can recommend this fine tip (#1) if you are seeking a very thin line - I use mine for Bible marking and notes. They come with a 3 month warranty. I’ve had them 4 months now and they haven’t dried up one bit. I’m happy with my purchase and will continue to buy their products.Love these! Would buy more if less $. Super thin tip! Great for notes & journaling.Great pens. They work great for my plannerI'm a huge fan of these pens. My latest order was just another re-up, and three months later I used the green pen for the first time and realized it was dried out and unusable. All the other pens so far have been fine.Lovely useful pensI had been looking for this item for some time, and anticipated a longer than normal delivery time, however the pens arrived early, in adequate packaging and met my expectations. They are just what I wanted and more.I’m using micron pens for fantasy mapping and they’ve been great! The archival quality and water proof ink allow me to use water color paint over the ink without the ink running or smudging, tho I allow 24 hours for ink to fully saturate and dry. When buying micron pens be mindful of the varying sizes and that some of the packets are all one size and some are mixed sizes. These are not pens for young children as the nibs can be wrecked if pressed too hard against the paper, require a deft touch. I’ve heard there are fake microns but I have not seen them and I would not know how to discern them other than I’ve heard they’re not waterproof.I love Sakura pigma micron pens but it's easy to mess them up. Especially if you're using them with different mediums. I clogged a tip because I wrote on top of acrylic gel medium. It *felt* dry but I guess not enough. That being said, I mostly use them on unadulterated paper so I'm okay.PS I managed to unclog the tip by immediately putting the tip in a cup of water then after a few minutes I shook it around, tapping the edges, pretty much what they say not to do. Ink started to come out into the water slowly. I dried the water off and I left it alone (cap on) for a few days. First try to use it again wasn't so good and I thought I failed but I came back to it another day and it gradually started flowing again. Fluke?I LOVE Sakura's Pigma Micron Pens!!!! They are pretty much as good as it gets! Archival quality ink, great pigma, comfortable to use, long lasting (for a disposable) At anywhere from about $2 - $2.75 per pen (Canadian dollars) You really get your money's worth....would have to buy 2 or 3 cheaper pens to do the job of one Micron...and the cheaper ones look worse and aren't archival!

top_review: This under sink 5 stage RO system went together easily with the help of the manual and is currently working quite well.  A number of little things, like the spare parts kit and the leak sensor cutoff switch are a nice touch.  The first stage sediment filter clear housing is a must and seems to only be included in this brand. Overall quality is excellent and the full color pictures with little installation hints were great.  Some minor howevers...However, there are a couple of items that can be improved, although they don't directly affect the performance of the system.  One is the sheer bulk of the system (and any other RO system of this design).  For dual sink installations where you have two sets of drains - and possibly garbage disposers, the system will not fit under the sink in all cases - mine was one.  The main problem is the pressure tank.  If you have a cabinet next door to the sink that you can give up some space, then the tank can go there.  Otherwise it could be a deal breaker.  This should be explained at the beginning of the manual and should give a footprint diagram and state: "STOP! Before you unpack our system...".  This could simply be an added sheet laying in the top of the package.Second, the tool list is basic and you'll need other tools depending on the installation.  Buy the optional slide-out rack is a must unless you plan to unmount the entire RO system occasionally as it will be impossible to change filters under the sink, especially the RO membrane.  I ended up installing mine in the utility room with the faucet mounted on my laundry sink.  This would be true of any RO system of this design.  Not something explained on Amazon web pages for any system I looked at.Third, the manual gives a great description on how to prepare the leak sensor feedwater cutoff device, but they omitted to tell you where to put it and which line to put it in.  I added the term "feedwater" because that's the line you put it in.  It should be placed in the bottom of the sink cabinet under the RO system to detect leaks from the various push-in connectors that wet the cabinet floor.  That should be thoroughly explained and seems to have been missed.Fourth, this system on my pressure well pump with 50-65 psi pressure switch, produces about 20 gallons a day, not 75 as advertised on Amazon.  Real specs are actually spelled out in the manual and are accurate there.  Not sure why they are advertising 75 GPD.  The RO water to waste water ratio is not 1.5:1, which sounds amazing.  It is closer to 1:1.5, which is closer to what I have read, about RO systems and is actually quite good for a non-boosted system.  Although this is what I expected, it is something to be aware of if you are using it heavily and are paying for your water.A note on the above performance:  my TDS (total dissolved solids) is lab tested at about 280 ppm for calcium compounds.  This is high, resulting in very hard water, and will slow down RO water production.  Also, running the system on a constant regulated higher pressure of 65 psi will improve the RO ratio and production performance.  If you're not sure the RO system is working, without a TDS meter, just taste the waste water. (be careful if you suspect high levels of contaminants).  Mine tastes like you dissolved a stick of chalk in it - imagined. The RO water is refreshing and clean.Overall, the system is excellent.  The USA based company is one reason I chose this system.  Although I have not had to use their help, other reviewers did and got good service.  I highly recommend this system and their USA based company iSpring.
